name: pdf-to-text
description: Extracts the plain text content from a PDF.
example_prompt: Pull all the text out of this PDF
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pypdf/pdfminer in the Python sandbox to parse the PDF locally.
rationale: Local PDF text extraction is a top Document demand and avoids leaking confidential docs.

name: speech-to-text-transcriber
description: Transcribes spoken audio into text using an in-browser Whisper model.
example_prompt: Transcribe this voice memo. <audio>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs Whisper fully in-browser (WASM/WebGPU); audio never leaves the device.
rationale: Delivers Dictation.io's core dictation feature locally, which is also a strong privacy selling point.

name: text-summarize
description: Produces a concise summary of a long passage of text.
example_prompt: Summarize this article in three sentences
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a distilled summarization model in-browser, no API key.
rationale: Private offline summarization is a flagship Study/Text demand for an AI chat app.

name: transcribe-audio
description: Generates a text transcript from speech in an audio or video file.
example_prompt: Transcribe this meeting recording to text
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a Whisper model fully in-browser (WebGPU/WASM), no API.
rationale: Private, free transcription is a flagship AI use case with enormous demand.

name: csv-json-convert
description: Converts tabular data between CSV and JSON in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this CSV to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — csv + serde_json parse and serialize entirely client-side.
rationale: CSV↔JSON is a top freetools/Online-Convert data task and keeps potentially sensitive datasets off any server.

name: grammar-checker
description: Corrects grammar and phrasing of a sentence or paragraph with a small text-to-text model.
example_prompt: fix the grammar: 'he go to store yesterday and buyed milk'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a compact grammar-correction seq2seq model in-browser.
rationale: PolishMyWriting demand is fundamentally about cleaning up writing without sending it to a server.

name: image-to-webp
description: Converts PNG, JPG, or BMP images to WebP with adjustable quality.
example_prompt: convert this PNG to WebP
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm) with libwebp encodes WebP entirely client-side via the wasmi bridge, no upload.
rationale: Direct match to the convert-to-webp demand term and a top web-performance optimization.

name: jpg-compressor
description: Re-encodes a JPG at a chosen quality level to reduce file size while keeping dimensions.
example_prompt: compress this jpg to about 200 KB
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm): quality-targeted MJPEG re-encoding runs client-side.
rationale: Shrinking JPGs for upload limits and web pages is one of the most common image chores.

name: ocr-image
description: Extracts readable text from an image, screenshot or scanned document using an on-device OCR model.
example_prompt: Pull the text out of this screenshot
loader_feasibility: transformers-js / onnx-runtime runs a TrOCR or PaddleOCR model via WASM/WebGPU, so the image is never uploaded.
rationale: OCR is high-demand and privacy-sensitive (IDs, receipts, contracts), making local execution a real differentiator.

name: pdf-compress
description: Shrinks a PDF by recompressing its streams and images.
example_prompt: Compress this PDF to make it smaller
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lopdf + image recompression) in-WASM.
rationale: Size reduction is the most-searched PDF utility and needs no server.

name: pdf-split
description: Extracts or splits out specific pages from a PDF.
example_prompt: Extract pages 2 to 5 from this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lopdf) page-tree editing.
rationale: Splitting PDFs locally keeps potentially sensitive documents off third-party servers.

name: remove-image-background
description: Removes the background from a photo, leaving a transparent cutout.
example_prompt: Remove the background from this product photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs an RMBG/U2Net segmentation model client-side via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Background removal is one of the highest-demand Graphics tools and usually paywalled.

name: text-to-image-generate
description: Generates an image from a text prompt using an on-device diffusion model.
example_prompt: Generate an image of a fox in a spacesuit
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a small Stable-Diffusion/Turbo model via WebGPU entirely in the browser.
rationale: Local, private text-to-image is a flagship capability that needs no API key or server cost.

name: text-translate
description: Translates text between languages offline.
example_prompt: Translate this paragraph into Spanish
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a small NLLB/Marian translation model in-browser, no API.
rationale: Private offline translation is a flagship Study/Communication demand for an AI chat app.

name: url-cleaner
description: Strips tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, etc.) from a URL to produce a clean shareable link.
example_prompt: Remove the tracking junk from this URL: <long url>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL parsing and query filtering; deterministic and offline.
rationale: The browser-local, privacy-positive slice of the Bitly/Dub link-management demand.

name: video-crop
description: Crops a video to a region or aspect ratio.
example_prompt: Crop this video to a square for Instagram
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg crop filter applies the region locally.
rationale: Aspect-ratio cropping for social platforms is a frequent edit and fully local.

name: add-audio-to-video
description: Adds or replaces the audio track of a video with an uploaded audio file.
example_prompt: put this song over my video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader muxes a new audio stream onto the video locally.
rationale: Adding background music to clips is a core editing task.

name: add-text-to-image
description: Overlays custom text (caption, watermark or meme) onto an image with position, font size and colour.
example_prompt: Add the caption 'SOLD' across the bottom of this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rasterizes glyphs with ab_glyph and composites onto the image in-memory.
rationale: Memes, watermarks and labelled screenshots are extremely common and need no design tool.

name: base64-file-converter
description: Converts an uploaded file to a Base64 data string and decodes a Base64 blob back into a downloadable file.
example_prompt: convert this image to a base64 data URI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — operates on the raw byte buffer handed in by the media-I/O page bridge; encoding is pure computation with no server round-trip.
rationale: Embedding small assets as data URIs and decoding pasted blobs are everyday tasks that should never need a remote server for privacy.

name: change-speed
description: Speeds up or slows down a video or audio file by a chosen factor, keeping audio in sync.
example_prompt: make this video play at 2x speed
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses setpts/atempo filters in the WASM build; all transcoding happens locally
rationale: Directly harvested change-speed demand; a frequent need for timelapses and condensed clips.

name: convert-image-format
description: Converts an image between PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF and TIFF with optional quality control.
example_prompt: Convert this PNG to a JPEG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image crate decodes and re-encodes locally.
rationale: Format conversion for compatibility and file size is one of the most-searched image tasks.

name: csv-to-json
description: Parses CSV (with header detection and delimiter options) into an array of JSON objects.
example_prompt: convert this CSV to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the csv + serde_json crates — pure parsing, no server
rationale: CSV→JSON is one of the highest-demand data conversions and benefits hugely from staying off any upload-based service.

name: docx-to-markdown
description: Extracts a Word .docx document into clean Markdown.
example_prompt: Convert this Word doc to markdown
loader_feasibility: pyodide sandbox running python-docx fully in-browser.
rationale: Covers the document-conversion side of Cloud Convert for editor workflows.

name: encrypt-file
description: Encrypts a file with a passphrase using AES-256-GCM, producing a portable encrypted blob.
example_prompt: Encrypt this file with a password before I send it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — aes-gcm and a KDF run in pure Rust with no server ever seeing the data.
rationale: Firefox Send's appeal was client-side-encrypted sharing; doing the encryption locally delivers that guarantee directly.

name: gif-to-mp4
description: Converts an animated GIF into a much smaller MP4/WebM video while preserving the loop.
example_prompt: convert this gif to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader re-encodes GIF frames to H.264/VP9 locally.
rationale: GIFs are huge; an MP4 is often 10x smaller for the same animation.

name: html-to-markdown
description: Converts an HTML fragment or page body into clean Markdown, preserving headings, links, lists, and code blocks.
example_prompt: turn this html into markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure-Rust HTML parsing mapped to Markdown emission, fully offline
rationale: Markdown is the lingua franca for docs and chat, so HTML-to-Markdown is a high-value conversion done locally.

name: html-to-text
description: Strips HTML markup to clean, readable plain text while preserving paragraph and list structure.
example_prompt: convert this html to plain text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `html2text` crate parses and renders without a browser DOM or network
rationale: Extracting readable text from HTML is a frequent preprocessing step for notes, scraping, and LLM input.

name: image-auto-tagger
description: Auto-labels an image with object/scene tags from a vision classifier.
example_prompt: What's in this photo? Tag it
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime web runs a MobileNet/ResNet ImageNet model entirely on-device via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Local image labeling powers search/organization without sending personal photos to a cloud API.

name: image-watermark
description: Overlays text or a logo watermark at a chosen position and opacity.
example_prompt: Add a semi-transparent '© 2026 Me' watermark to the bottom-right
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; compose layers and rasterize text with `ab_glyph` + a bundled font.
rationale: Watermarking is a recurring BeFunky/Pixlr task and fully expressible as local pixel compositing.

name: images-to-pdf
description: Combines a set of images into a single PDF, one image per page.
example_prompt: Make a PDF from these scanned photos
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — printpdf/lopdf embed images and emit the PDF locally.
rationale: JPG/PNG-to-PDF is among the top Online Convert queries and is straightforward to keep on-device.

name: jpg-to-png
description: Converts JPG images to lossless PNG.
example_prompt: convert this jpg to png
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm): JPEG decode + PNG encode run fully in-browser.
rationale: Needed whenever a lossless or editing-friendly format is required, the natural inverse of image-to-jpg.

name: line-series-chart
description: Renders a line/time-series chart from one or more numeric series as an SVG or PNG.
example_prompt: Chart these monthly sales numbers as a line graph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (plotters SVG backend) draws the chart locally.
rationale: Turning pasted tables and time series into a shareable chart is a frequent, offline-friendly task.

name: pdf-rotate
description: Rotates or reorders pages within a PDF.
example_prompt: Rotate every page in this PDF 90 degrees
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lopdf) page attribute edits.
rationale: Common quick fix bundled into PdfEscape-style editors.

name: readability-extractor
description: Extracts the main article content from cluttered pasted HTML, stripping nav, ads and boilerplate.
example_prompt: clean this page HTML down to just the article text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs a Readability-style heuristic over the parsed DOM locally.
rationale: PrintWhatYouLike demand maps to decluttering page content for reading or printing.

name: readable-article
description: Strips navigation, ads, and clutter from pasted article HTML to produce a clean reader/print view.
example_prompt: Clean up this article HTML so it's print friendly
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — html5ever plus a readability heuristic extracts the main content locally.
rationale: Print Friendly's core value is decluttering, which is a deterministic HTML transform that runs in-browser.

name: resume-builder
description: Turns structured details (contact, experience, skills) into a clean, ATS-friendly Markdown resume.
example_prompt: Build a resume from this info: name, 3 jobs, skills... <details>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating of user-supplied fields into formatted text; fully offline.
rationale: Maps Resume Nation to a deterministic formatter that keeps a user's private CV data entirely on-device.

name: safelink-decoder
description: Unwraps Outlook SafeLinks, Proofpoint, Google and other URL-rewrite wrappers to reveal the original destination.
example_prompt: decode this safelink: https://nam.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the wrapper query string and percent-decodes the embedded target; no navigation or fetch required.
rationale: Seeing the true destination of a rewritten link is a security-relevant task best done without actually visiting the URL.

name: subtitle-translator
description: Translates the text lines of an .srt/.vtt subtitle file into another language while preserving timestamps.
example_prompt: Translate this .srt file from English to Spanish. <srt>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust parses the cues offline; transformers-js translates each line in-browser via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Maps the dubbing/translation reading of Dub into a concrete, fully-local localization tool.

name: toxicity-classifier
description: Scores text for toxicity/harassment likelihood with a small classification model.
example_prompt: how toxic is this message: 'you always ruin everything'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a small toxic-comment classifier fully in the browser.
rationale: A model-based companion to the wordlist filter for nuanced 'word safety' checks.

name: trim-audio
description: Extracts or removes a time range from an audio file to keep just the part you want.
example_prompt: cut this mp3 to just the first 30 seconds
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader seeks and slices audio streams locally.
rationale: Quick audio trims (ringtones, clips) are a high-frequency need.

name: video-convert
description: Converts video between mp4, webm, mov and mkv.
example_prompt: Convert this mov to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM transcodes containers/codecs in the browser.
rationale: Container/codec conversion is a top VideoToolbox request and avoids slow uploads.

name: video-merge
description: Concatenates multiple video clips into one.
example_prompt: Join these clips into a single video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg concat joins compatible streams locally in WASM.
rationale: Stitching clips is a core editing task and keeps large source files off any server.

name: video-mute
description: Removes the audio track from a video.
example_prompt: Mute this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg -an strips the audio stream client-side.
rationale: Muting is a quick VideoToolbox edit with no need to upload the file.

name: video-resize
description: Scales a video to a target resolution.
example_prompt: Resize this video to 720p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg scale filter rescales frames locally in WASM.
rationale: Resolution changes are routine for platform requirements and are cheap client-side.

name: video-rotate
description: Rotates or flips a video.
example_prompt: Rotate this clip 90 degrees clockwise
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg transpose/hflip filters rotate frames in WASM.
rationale: Fixing sideways phone videos is a common annoyance solved instantly on-device.

name: video-to-frames
description: Extracts still frames from a video at a chosen interval as PNGs.
example_prompt: Grab one frame per second from this clip as images
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg frame export runs locally and returns image buffers to the chat.
rationale: Frame extraction feeds thumbnails, contact sheets, and ML datasets — common and offline-friendly.

name: audio-convert
description: Converts audio between mp3, wav, ogg, flac, and m4a.
example_prompt: Convert this wav file to mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg handles all codecs in its WASM build with no network round-trip.
rationale: Format conversion is the backbone of the File-Converters and Music categories.

name: audio-normalize
description: Levels an audio file to a standard loudness so volume is consistent.
example_prompt: Normalize the loudness of this podcast episode
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loudnorm (EBU R128) filter computes and applies gain locally.
rationale: Podcasters and musicians need consistent loudness and currently rely on paid web tools.

name: audio-silence-remove
description: Strips long silent gaps out of a recording.
example_prompt: Remove the dead air from this voice memo
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg silenceremove filter detects and cuts silence locally.
rationale: Voice-memo and podcast cleanup is repetitive manual work this automates privately.

name: audio-to-mono
description: Downmixes stereo or multi-channel audio to a single mono channel.
example_prompt: convert this stereo file to mono
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm): channel downmix is a local re-encode in the browser.
rationale: Mono conversion is a standard prep step for speech and embedded-device audio.

name: audio-volume-adjust
description: Increases or decreases the gain of an audio file by a specified dB or factor.
example_prompt: make this recording 6 dB louder
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm): the volume filter re-encodes locally with no upload.
rationale: Quiet recordings are extremely common and a one-shot gain bump is a frequent request.

name: basic-auth-header-generator
description: Builds an HTTP Basic Authorization header value from a username and password.
example_prompt: make a basic auth header for user admin password s3cret
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — concatenate and Base64-encode credentials; deterministic and offline, keeping secrets off any network.
rationale: Credentials should never be pasted into an online generator, so a local tool is both convenient and safer.

name: burn-subtitles
description: Hard-burns an SRT subtitle file onto a video.
example_prompt: Burn these subtitles into the video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg subtitles filter renders the captions onto frames locally.
rationale: Burned-in captions are required for social video and avoid uploading the source clip.

name: censor-text
description: Redacts a supplied list of words (or common profanity) by masking them with asterisks.
example_prompt: censor the swear words in this comment
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenize-and-mask; local CPU, no model required
rationale: Quick redaction before sharing screenshots/quotes is a real privacy chore.

name: correlation-heatmap
description: Computes a Pearson/Spearman correlation matrix across numeric CSV columns and renders it as a labeled heatmap.
example_prompt: Show me a correlation heatmap of the numeric columns in this dataset
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes correlations and renders SVG entirely in-memory, so it runs client-side on the wasmi runtime.
rationale: Correlation heatmaps are a staple of exploratory data analysis and require no external libraries beyond basic stats.

name: create-zip
description: Bundles multiple uploaded files into a single downloadable ZIP archive.
example_prompt: Zip these three files together for me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the zip crate's writer assembling the archive in memory.
rationale: Simple, frequently-wanted utility that complements the extract tools and needs no backend.

name: csv-change-delimiter
description: Re-saves a CSV with a different separator (comma, tab, semicolon, pipe) and proper requoting.
example_prompt: change this csv to use semicolons
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse and re-serialize, no network.
rationale: Delimiter mismatches between tools are a constant source of import errors.

name: csv-dedupe
description: Removes duplicate rows from a CSV, optionally keyed on chosen columns.
example_prompt: Remove duplicate rows from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashing and row comparison.
rationale: A frequent spreadsheet cleanup task that EtherCalc users hit constantly.

name: csv-filter
description: Filters CSV rows by a conditional expression over column values.
example_prompt: Keep only rows where amount > 100 and status == 'paid'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM expression evaluator over parsed rows; fully in-memory.
rationale: Conditional row selection is a core spreadsheet operation that's clumsy without formulas.

name: csv-formula-eval
description: Evaluates spreadsheet-style formulas to add or transform CSV columns.
example_prompt: Add a column equal to price times quantity to this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM expression engine; all evaluation in-WASM.
rationale: Formula evaluation is EtherCalc's whole reason to exist.

name: csv-group-by
description: Groups CSV rows by a chosen column and aggregates others (count, sum, average) per group.
example_prompt: group this csv by category and sum the amount
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse and aggregation, fully local.
rationale: Group-and-aggregate is the most common spreadsheet-style summarization.

name: csv-group-split
description: Forks one CSV into multiple files, one per distinct value in a chosen key column.
example_prompt: Split this orders.csv into one file per country column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse + group-by; deterministic in-memory partitioning, no backend.
rationale: Per-segment exports are a frequent spreadsheet chore that's tedious to do by hand.

name: csv-insert-column
description: Adds a new column to a CSV at a chosen position, filled with a constant or a per-row template.
example_prompt: add an id column to this csv
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse and rewrite, no server.
rationale: Inserting columns is a common pre-processing step before import.

name: csv-merge
description: Concatenates or key-joins multiple CSV files into a single unified table.
example_prompt: Merge these three monthly CSVs into one, matching on the email column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse + join/union in memory; entirely browser-local.
rationale: Combining exports from different sources is one of the most common spreadsheet pains.

name: csv-pivot
description: Builds a pivot table that groups and aggregates a CSV.
example_prompt: Pivot this CSV: sum sales by region
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM grouping and aggregation.
rationale: Pivoting is the most-wanted advanced spreadsheet operation.

name: csv-query
description: Runs SQL-style SELECT, filter, and aggregate queries over CSV data.
example_prompt: Select rows where amount > 100 from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM in-memory query engine.
rationale: Turns a flat sheet into a queryable dataset entirely client-side.

name: csv-to-tsv
description: Converts CSV text into tab-separated values, correctly handling quoted fields and embedded delimiters.
example_prompt: convert this CSV to TSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RFC-4180 CSV parse + TSV emit is pure string/state-machine work with no network, runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Direct hit on a common spreadsheet-export conversion that people currently paste into sketchy online converters.

name: decrypt-file
description: Decrypts a passphrase-encrypted file produced by the encrypt-file tool.
example_prompt: Decrypt this encrypted file with my password
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AES-GCM decryption runs entirely client-side.
rationale: The necessary counterpart to encrypt-file, completing a private, serverless Firefox-Send-style exchange.

name: detect-file-type
description: Identifies a file's true format by inspecting its magic bytes and header structure regardless of the extension.
example_prompt: What kind of file is this actually? Detect its real type.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; magic-byte signature matching is pure byte inspection with no network or system calls.
rationale: Mislabeled extensions and file-type confusion are everywhere, and a private offline sniffer is broadly useful.

name: extract-audio-from-video
description: Pulls the audio track out of a video file as MP3 or WAV.
example_prompt: Extract the audio from this mp4 as an mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg demuxes and re-encodes the audio stream in-browser via the WASM build.
rationale: Common 'rip the audio' task that keeps private media off any server.

name: extract-pdf-images
description: Extracts the embedded raster images from a PDF and returns them as downloadable PNG/JPEG files.
example_prompt: extract all images from this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pulls image XObjects from the object graph and decodes them with the pure-Rust image crate; no page rasterization or server needed.
rationale: Maps extract-images-from-pdf using only structural extraction, which is reliably feasible browser-local.

name: extract-tar
description: Lists and extracts files from tar, tar.gz and tgz archives in the browser.
example_prompt: Extract this tar.gz and list the files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via tar + flate2/miniz_oxide; decompression runs locally.
rationale: Windows users especially lack an easy tar.gz opener and won't want to upload archives.

name: file-encryptor
description: Password-encrypts and decrypts an entire file with authenticated AES-GCM.
example_prompt: Encrypt this PDF with a password
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM AES-GCM over the file bytes locally; nothing is uploaded.
rationale: The same privacy demand as the text encryptors extends to whole files people want protected before sharing.

name: file-hash
description: Computes MD5, SHA-1, and SHA-256 checksums of any file for integrity checks and threat-intel lookups.
example_prompt: What's the SHA-256 hash of this file?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with pure-Rust hash crates; hashing runs over the local buffer.
rationale: Hashing is core to file verification and matching indicators of compromise, and needs to be exact and offline.

name: file-splitter
description: Splits a large text or CSV file into N equal parts or fixed-size chunks.
example_prompt: Split this 50MB CSV into 5 separate files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM slices the buffer on line/size boundaries; all client-side memory ops.
rationale: Many upload tools and importers cap file size, so a private local splitter saves real friction.

name: file-to-data-uri
description: Encodes a small file as a self-contained base64 data: URI for inline embedding.
example_prompt: Turn this small image into a data URI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — base64 encoding plus MIME detection is a trivial local transform.
rationale: Self-contained inline assets are the serverless answer to RGhost/EFShare hotlinking and are instant to generate.

name: find-replace
description: Finds and replaces text using literal or regular-expression matching, with case and global options.
example_prompt: replace all 'foo' with 'bar' in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the regex crate; matching and substitution run locally.
rationale: Bulk find/replace is one of the most universally requested text operations.

name: generate-rsa-key-pair
description: Generates an RSA key pair of a chosen size (2048/3072/4096) and outputs PEM public and private keys.
example_prompt: Generate a 2048-bit RSA key pair
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the rsa crate; the new private key is created inside the sandbox and never sent anywhere.
rationale: Generating RSA keys without installing OpenSSL is broadly useful, and locality is essential for private-key safety.

name: gunzip
description: Decompresses a gzip (.gz) file or blob back to its original bytes or text.
example_prompt: decompress this .gz dump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via flate2 — inflate is pure Rust and runs client-side with no upload.
rationale: Reading .gz payloads locally avoids uploading sensitive logs or dumps to an online decompressor.

name: heatmap-chart
description: Renders a numeric matrix or CSV grid as a color-coded heatmap with optional per-cell value labels and a color legend.
example_prompt: Make a heatmap from this CSV of monthly sales by region
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the matrix, maps values to a colormap, and emits an SVG string — pure text output, no server or GPU needed.
rationale: Heatmaps are one of the most-requested chart types and a plain matrix-to-SVG renderer covers the core demand with minimal effort.

name: html-table-extractor
description: Extracts tables from pasted HTML and outputs them as CSV or JSON.
example_prompt: pull the tables out of this HTML and give me CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the HTML DOM and serializes rows locally.
rationale: Dataflow-kit demand reflects need to scrape structured tables, here done on pasted markup without a server.

name: image-collage
description: Combines several images into a single grid, strip, or side-by-side collage.
example_prompt: Stitch these 6 screenshots into a 2x3 grid image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM `image` crate composites pixels on a canvas buffer; fully in-page.
rationale: Quick collages/contact sheets are a recurring need that usually means uploading photos to a website.

name: image-color-picker
description: Reports the hex/RGB color at a given pixel coordinate in an image.
example_prompt: What hex color is at the center of this image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; decode and sample a pixel, no network.
rationale: Eyedropper sampling is a recurring design need shared by PhotoPea and the color tools.

name: image-info
description: Reports an image's dimensions, format, color type, and file size without uploading it.
example_prompt: what are the dimensions of this png?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the PNG/JPEG/GIF header bytes; reads the file locally, no decode needed
rationale: The png demand maps to a quick metadata peek that's annoying to get otherwise.

name: image-pixelate-censor
description: Pixelates or blurs a chosen region to censor faces or sensitive info.

name: video-frame-grab
description: Extracts a single still frame from a video at a chosen timestamp as a PNG or JPEG.
example_prompt: Grab a thumbnail from this video at 5 seconds
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg seeks and decodes one frame entirely client-side, no upload of the full clip.
rationale: Poster frames and thumbnails are a constant need and keep private video on-device.

name: video-to-gif
description: Converts a section of a video into an optimized animated GIF.
example_prompt: Make a gif from the first 4 seconds of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg palettegen/paletteuse filter chain runs entirely client-side in WASM.
rationale: GIF-from-video is a perennial high-volume converter request that needs no server.

name: vocal-remover
description: Removes center-panned vocals to create a karaoke/instrumental track.
example_prompt: Remove the vocals from this song
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg pan/stereo-difference filtering cancels the center channel locally; no model needed.
rationale: AI Vocal Remover demand is huge and the center-cancel method runs instantly client-side.

name: word-frequency
description: Counts and ranks the most frequently used words in a block of text.
example_prompt: what are the 10 most common words in this article?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenize-and-tally with a stopword list; pure CPU in the sandbox
rationale: Surfacing keyword distribution maps the statistic demand to a useful writing/SEO aid.

name: word-frequency-counter
description: Counts how often each word appears and ranks them, with optional stop-word filtering.
example_prompt: What are the most common words in this text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenize and hash-map count entirely client-side.
rationale: Extends text-statistics demand; useful for SEO and writing analysis.

name: xml-to-csv
description: Flattens repeated XML elements into a CSV table with columns inferred from child tags and attributes.
example_prompt: convert this XML list of products into a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse + flatten + CSV-encode are all pure text operations, browser-local.
rationale: Turns API/feed XML into spreadsheet-ready data, a common analyst workflow.

name: xml-to-json
description: Converts an XML document into an equivalent JSON structure preserving attributes and nesting.
example_prompt: convert this xml to json: <user id="1"><name>Ana</name></user>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — quick-xml plus serde_json do the parse and emit purely in memory, fully offline.
rationale: Bridging legacy XML feeds into JSON tooling is a constant integration chore worth a one-shot converter.

name: xml-validator
description: Checks XML for well-formedness and, if an XSD is provided, validates against the schema, reporting line/column of errors.
example_prompt: validate this XML and tell me what's wrong
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a pure-Rust XML parser walks the document in memory; no server or DTD network fetch.
rationale: Directly fulfills the xml-validator demand and keeps potentially sensitive XML payloads on-device.

name: yaml-to-json
description: Parses YAML into equivalent JSON, preserving types and nested structures.
example_prompt: convert this YAML to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via serde_yaml + serde_json — pure parsing, no network
rationale: Config-file conversion between YAML and JSON is a daily devops task with strong recurring demand.

name: yara-scan
description: Runs user-supplied YARA rules against an uploaded file and reports which rules and strings matched.
example_prompt: Run these YARA rules against this file and tell me what matches.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust yara-x engine; rule compilation and matching execute locally with no scanner backend.
rationale: Lets analysts triage suspicious files privately without uploading samples to a cloud sandbox.

name: animated-heatmap
description: Takes a time-ordered sequence of matrices and renders an animated heatmap (GIF/MP4) showing how values evolve.
example_prompt: Animate these hourly traffic matrices into a heatmap GIF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM renders each frame to a bitmap and the ffmpeg loader encodes the GIF/MP4 — both run client-side in WASM.
rationale: Animated heatmaps convey temporal change that a single static frame cannot, and ffmpeg makes local encoding straightforward.

name: animated-webp-to-gif
description: Converts animated WebP files back to GIF for maximum compatibility.
example_prompt: convert this animated WebP to a GIF
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm): decodes animated WebP frames and encodes a GIF locally.
rationale: GIF remains the universally-accepted animation format for chats and docs, so the reverse path is in demand.

name: audio-concat
description: Merges multiple audio clips into one continuous track with optional crossfade.
example_prompt: Join these three voice memos into one MP3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (WASM build) concat/filter runs in-browser, decoding and re-encoding locally.
rationale: Stitching audio is a frequent podcast/voice-note task and avoids uploading private recordings.

name: audio-metadata-editor
description: Views and edits ID3 tags (title, artist, album, year) and embedded cover art on an audio file.
example_prompt: Set the artist and album tags on this MP3
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM ID3 read/write on the uploaded bytes; no server.
rationale: Music collected from radio/streaming sources arrives with missing or wrong tags that listeners want to fix.

name: base32-codec
description: Encodes text or bytes to RFC 4648 Base32 and decodes Base32 strings back to the original data.
example_prompt: base32 encode "secret token"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 5-bit group packing is pure bit arithmetic.
rationale: Base32 is widely used for TOTP secrets and case-insensitive identifiers, with explicit two-way demand.

name: bcrypt-hash
description: Generates a bcrypt hash for a password at a chosen cost and verifies a password against an existing bcrypt hash.
example_prompt: Make a bcrypt hash of 'p@ssw0rd' at cost 12, and check it against $2b$12$...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure-Rust bcrypt implementation runs deterministically with no network.
rationale: Developers constantly generate and verify bcrypt hashes and want to avoid pasting passwords into web tools.

name: bip39-mnemonic-generator
description: Generates a BIP39 mnemonic seed phrase (12–24 words) from secure entropy with checksum.
example_prompt: generate a 24-word bip39 mnemonic
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the bip39 crate and getrandom for entropy; the phrase is created locally and never sent anywhere.
rationale: Seed phrases must be generated offline for safety, making a browser-local wasm tool exactly the right delivery.

name: blowfish-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with Blowfish in ECB or CBC mode with PKCS7 padding.
example_prompt: Encrypt this string with Blowfish-CBC using key 'p@ss' and this IV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `blowfish` + `cbc` crates; block-cipher rounds are pure compute with no network.
rationale: Blowfish is still embedded in older databases and appliances, so decoding its output is a real interop need.

name: blur-image
description: Applies a Gaussian blur of adjustable radius to an entire image.
example_prompt: Blur this image a lot
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image/imageproc convolves locally; webgpu-compute shader optional for large images.
rationale: Blurring for privacy redaction and soft backgrounds is common and shouldn't require an upload.

name: bollinger-bands
description: Computes Bollinger Bands (moving average plus/minus standard deviations).
example_prompt: Compute Bollinger Bands for these closes with a 20 period
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the mean/stddev bands on pasted data.
rationale: Bollinger Bands round out the common TradingView indicator set, all client-side.

name: byte-drop
description: Removes a byte range (start offset + length) from text, hex, or base64 input and returns the remainder.
example_prompt: drop bytes 0 through 7 from this hex blob
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; in-memory byte removal, fully client-side.
rationale: The inverse of byte-take, useful for stripping headers/magic bytes before further analysis.

name: bzip2-compress
description: Compresses input using the bzip2 (Burrows–Wheeler) algorithm, usually smaller than gzip on text.
example_prompt: bzip2 compress this text file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust libbz2-rs-sys port — no C toolchain, runs in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: bzip2 gives better ratios on text than gzip and there is no good offline browser tool for producing it.

name: change-case
description: Converts text to UPPER, lower, Title, Sentence, or swapped case.
example_prompt: make this paragraph all uppercase
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ASCII/Unicode case mapping is a pure in-memory transform with no network or filesystem dependency.
rationale: Covers the high-frequency To Upper / To Lower / Swap case demand in a single intuitive tool.

name: chi-square-test
description: Runs a chi-square goodness-of-fit or contingency-table test and reports the statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value.
example_prompt: run a chi-square test on observed 10,20,30 vs expected 20,20,20
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — chi-square statistic plus an incomplete-gamma p-value approximation, pure math
rationale: A self-contained statistical test is broadly useful for data analysis and demanded both in stats and cryptanalysis contexts.

name: code-comment-generator
description: Generates docstrings or inline comments explaining a code snippet.
example_prompt: Add comments and a docstring to this Python function
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a small instruct/code model fully in-browser via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: On-device code commenting helps documentation without sending proprietary code to an external API.

name: code-to-image
description: Renders a syntax-highlighted code snippet into a polished PNG image for sharing.
example_prompt: Make a nice image of this Python function to post on Twitter
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM highlights with syntect and rasterizes glyphs and background to pixels locally.
rationale: Shareable code screenshots (à la carbon.now.sh) are extremely popular among developers.

name: color-palette-extract
description: Extracts the dominant color palette from an image as hex codes.
example_prompt: Pull the main colors out of this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM k-means/quantization over pixels runs instantly client-side.
rationale: Designers constantly need palettes from reference images; cheap and offline.

name: color-palette-generator
description: Generates harmonious palettes (complementary, analogous, triadic, split) from a base color.
example_prompt: Give me a triadic palette based on #3B82F6
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; HSL color-wheel math, no I/O.
rationale: Palette generation is the core of Coolors/Adobe Color/Branition and is pure math.

name: css-autoprefixer
description: Adds vendor prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-, -ms-) to pasted CSS for the properties that still need them.
example_prompt: add vendor prefixes to this css: .box { display: flex; user-select: none; }
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS tokenizing with an embedded prefix-rules table; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Direct match for CSS Autoprefixer demand with no build-tool setup.

name: css-selector-extract
description: Extracts elements, text, or attributes from an HTML document using a CSS selector.
example_prompt: Pull the text of every a.headline from this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via scraper (html5ever + selectors), parsing the supplied HTML locally.
rationale: Scraper-builders need to test selectors against saved HTML without spinning up Node or a headless browser.

name: csv-find-incomplete-rows
description: Flags CSV rows that have too few or too many fields or contain blank required cells.
example_prompt: find the broken rows in this csv
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM field-count and emptiness validation, fully local.
rationale: Catching malformed rows before import saves a lot of downstream debugging.

name: data-uri-decode
description: Decodes a data: URI into its MIME type and decoded payload, with a text preview or downloadable bytes.
example_prompt: Decode this data URI: data:text/plain;base64,SGVsbG8=
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: parse the data: scheme then base64/percent-decode the body, entirely client-side.
rationale: Data URIs embed a MIME type plus encoded content and turn up in CSS, HTML, and JSON, so decoding them locally reveals what they actually contain.

name: date-diff
description: Computes the duration between two dates broken down into years, months, days, hours, and total units.
example_prompt: how many days between 2026-01-01 and 2026-06-19
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date subtraction and unit breakdown are pure calendar math executed client-side.
rationale: Directly fulfills the time-between-dates demand, a perennial planning and billing calculation.

name: dot-to-svg
description: Renders Graphviz DOT diagram source into an SVG.
example_prompt: Draw this graph from DOT source
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM layout engine; no Graphviz binary or server.
rationale: Captures Draw.io-style diagram demand from a text spec, runnable offline.

name: email-normalizer
description: Canonicalizes an email address by lowercasing, stripping Gmail dots and plus-tags, and reporting the deliverable form.
example_prompt: normalize First.Last+news@Gmail.com
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string parsing with provider-specific rules; no DNS or SMTP lookup so it is fully browser-local.
rationale: De-duplicating sign-ups and detecting alias abuse needs canonical emails, and doing it offline avoids leaking address lists.

name: email-validator
description: Validates email-address syntax against RFC rules and flags common typos and formatting issues.
example_prompt: Is 'jane.doe@@example..com' a valid email address?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM syntactic validation; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Adjacent to Mailinator/Randommer email needs and a perennially useful, fully local check.

name: error-level-analysis
description: Performs Error Level Analysis by recompressing a JPEG and amplifying the differences to reveal edited or spliced regions.
example_prompt: Run error level analysis on this photo to check if it's been edited.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; JPEG recompression and pixel-difference amplification run locally with the image crate.
rationale: ELA is the most popular quick check for image tampering and has clear demand but few trustworthy offline tools.

name: extract-domains
description: Extracts hostnames and registrable domains from text, URLs, or emails and lists them deduplicated.
example_prompt: List the unique domains referenced in this threat report
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing + public-suffix matching bundled in the WASM; offline.
rationale: Threat-intel and SEO users frequently need a clean domain inventory from messy text.

name: extract-exif
description: Reads EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata (camera, lens, exposure, timestamps) from a photo.
example_prompt: What camera and settings were used for this photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the kamadak-exif parser reading the uploaded image's headers; no decode, no upload.
rationale: Photographers and investigators want metadata without handing their image to an online EXIF site.

name: fake-data-generator
description: Generates rows of fake test records (name, email, phone, address) as CSV or JSON.
example_prompt: Generate 20 fake user records as CSV with name, email, and phone.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sampling from embedded datasets with a seed; serialization is offline.
rationale: The broad Randommer 'mock data' use case, valuable to developers and fully self-contained.

name: fernet-token
description: Creates or reads Fernet tokens (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256), with optional TTL verification on decrypt.
example_prompt: Make a Fernet token for this message using this base64 key, then decode it back
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `fernet` crate; AES, HMAC, and base64url are all pure compute with no network.
rationale: Fernet is the default token format in Python's `cryptography` library, so devs constantly need to mint and inspect them.

name: find-unique-lines
description: Returns only the lines that appear exactly once across the input.
example_prompt: show me the lines that only appear once
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM frequency count over lines, no server.
rationale: Isolating one-off entries is distinct from dedupe and useful for diffing lists.

name: frequency-distribution
description: Builds a character, byte, or n-gram frequency table (with counts and percentages) from input text or hex.
example_prompt: show me the letter frequency of this ciphertext
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hashmap counting over input bytes, no dependencies
rationale: Frequency tables underpin nearly all classical cryptanalysis and quick data profiling, and need no server.

name: fuzzy-hash
description: Computes an SSDEEP context-triggered piecewise hash (CTPH) of a file, producing a similarity-comparable fingerprint.
example_prompt: generate the ssdeep fuzzy hash of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a pure-Rust ssdeep implementation reads file bytes locally and computes the rolling/piecewise hash entirely in wasmi.
rationale: Fuzzy hashing is the core of malware-similarity and near-duplicate detection and there is almost no browser-local SSDEEP tool, mapping the 'SSDEEP'/'CTPH' demand precisely.

name: generate-ecdsa-key-pair
description: Generates an ECDSA key pair on a chosen curve (P-256/P-384/P-521) and outputs PEM and optionally JWK keys.
example_prompt: Generate a P-256 ECDSA key pair
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the p256/p384 + ecdsa crates; the private key is generated locally and never transmitted.
rationale: EC keys back most modern JWT/mTLS setups and generating them locally avoids exposing the private key.

name: generate-hotp
description: Computes a counter-based HOTP code from a Base32 secret and counter value, with configurable digits.
example_prompt: generate the hotp code for secret JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP at counter 5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HMAC over the counter, identical primitives to TOTP, fully offline
rationale: HOTP covers hardware-token and event-based OTP scenarios that TOTP does not, completing the OTP toolset.

name: geojson-to-svg
description: Renders GeoJSON features into an SVG map without tile servers.
example_prompt: Draw this GeoJSON as a map
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM projection and SVG emit; no external map tiles needed.
rationale: Delivers ScribbleMaps-style shape drawing fully client-side.

name: gif-reverse
description: Reverses the playback order of an animated GIF.
example_prompt: Reverse this GIF so it plays backwards
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader; `reverse` filter on the frame stream, client-side.
rationale: Reversing is a fun, popular ezGIF effect and cheap to implement locally.

name: gpx-analyzer
description: Parses a GPX track and reports distance, elevation gain, duration and pace.
example_prompt: analyze this GPX file and tell me total distance and elevation gain
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses XML and does the geodesic math locally.
rationale: Mapping/cartography users (Abc-Map) often need to inspect their own track files privately.

name: gzip-size-estimator
description: Reports the raw and gzipped byte size of pasted code or text to estimate transfer weight.
example_prompt: How big is this JS bundle gzipped?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM — flate2 gzip-compresses the input locally to measure size, no network.
rationale: Maps Pingdom/Website Speed Test 'how heavy is my page' demand onto the one part that is computable locally — compressed asset size.

name: hash-identifier
description: Identifies the likely hash or MAC scheme of a string (bcrypt, Argon2, NT, LM, MD5, SHA-family, CRC, and more).
example_prompt: What kind of hash is $2b$12$abcd...?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; identification is local pattern, length, and prefix matching.
rationale: Figuring out what a mystery hash is precedes any cracking or migration task and is a common first step.

name: hash-text
description: Computes a cryptographic hash of any pasted text using a selectable algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA3, BLAKE3, and more).
example_prompt: sha256 hash of "hello world"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RustCrypto digest crates (md-5, sha1, sha2, sha3, blake3) are pure-Rust, deterministic and CPU-only, so they run entirely in the wasmi runtime with no network.
rationale: A single multi-algorithm text hasher is the highest-traffic catch-all that satisfies most 'generate a hash' intents in one tool.

name: hmac-generate
description: Computes a keyed HMAC of a message using a selectable underlying hash (HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA1, HMAC-SHA512, etc.).
example_prompt: hmac-sha256 of "payload" with key "secret"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the hmac crate composes over RustCrypto digests, all pure-Rust and deterministic in wasmi.
rationale: HMAC is the most common real-world use of these hash primitives (webhook signing, API auth) and is a natural high-value extension of the hashing tool family.

name: html-beautify
description: Indents and tidies HTML markup, normalizing nesting and attribute spacing.
example_prompt: beautify this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via an HTML5 tokenizer (html5ever) reserialized with indentation; client-side only.
rationale: Generic code-beautify demand maps cleanly to HTML, the most-pasted unformatted markup.

name: iban-validator
description: Validates an IBAN via the mod-97 checksum and parses out country, bank and account components.
example_prompt: validate IBAN DE89370400440532013000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — checksum arithmetic and a bundled country-format table run entirely in the sandbox.
rationale: Validating bank details locally is essential for privacy since IBANs are sensitive financial data.

name: identify-archive-format
description: Detects the compression or archive format of an uploaded blob from its magic bytes (gzip, zlib, bzip2, xz/LZMA, zip, tar, LZ4, and more).
example_prompt: what compression format is this file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure magic-byte sniffing over the buffer, fully client-side with no upload.
rationale: Users often have an unknown compressed blob and need to know which decompressor to reach for before doing anything else.

name: image-contain-fit
description: Fits an image inside target dimensions preserving aspect ratio, padding the remainder with a chosen colour (letterbox).
example_prompt: Fit this into a 1080x1080 square with white padding
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resizes then composites onto a padded canvas in-memory.
rationale: Social platforms demand fixed canvas sizes and 'contain' avoids cropping any content.

name: image-cover-fit
description: Scales and centre-crops an image to completely fill target dimensions while preserving aspect ratio.
example_prompt: Make this fill a 16:9 banner
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resizes then crops the overflow locally.
rationale: Hero and banner images need exact dimensions with no letterboxing — the inverse of contain.

name: image-false-color
description: Maps a grayscale or thermal image's luminance through a scientific colormap to produce a false-color heatmap image.
example_prompt: Apply a thermal heatmap colormap to this grayscale X-ray image
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes/encodes the image while the per-pixel colormap mapping is pure Rust — all in the browser's WASM sandbox.
rationale: False-color heatmapping makes grayscale, depth, and thermal imagery readable and is a common image-processing ask.

name: image-opacity
description: Sets or scales the alpha/opacity of an image, producing a semi-transparent PNG.
example_prompt: Make this logo 50% transparent
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rewrites the alpha channel in-memory.
rationale: Watermarks and overlay assets need adjustable transparency without a full editor.

name: image-to-sketch
description: Turns a photo into a pencil or line-art sketch.
example_prompt: Make this photo look like a pencil sketch
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg edge-detection and blend filters compiled to WASM.
rationale: Captures the Sketchpad/kleki drawing aesthetic as a one-shot transform.

name: index-of-coincidence
description: Calculates the Index of Coincidence for text to gauge whether it is monoalphabetic, polyalphabetic, or random.
example_prompt: what's the index of coincidence of this text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — simple combinatorial sum over letter counts
rationale: IoC is a standard cipher-classification metric that pairs naturally with the other cryptanalysis tools.

name: ioc-defang
description: Defangs or refangs IOCs (URLs, IP addresses, domains and emails) by neutralizing or restoring schemes, dots and at-signs.
example_prompt: Defang this URL and IP so I can paste them safely: http://evil.example.com/path and 203.0.113.45
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reversible pattern substitution (http→hxxp, .→[.], @→[at]) on text; no network and trivially bidirectional.
rationale: Defanging is a daily must for sharing malicious indicators safely in reports and chat, covering the Defang URL, Fang URL and Defang IP demand in one tool.

name: ioc-extract
description: Extracts indicators of compromise — IPv4/IPv6, URLs, domains, emails and MD5/SHA hashes — from an arbitrary block of text and optionally defangs them.
example_prompt: Pull all the IPs, domains and hashes out of this incident report text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex scanning over the input string; entirely local with no calls out.
rationale: Bulk-harvesting indicators from logs and reports is the natural front end to defanging and a high-value analyst workflow.

name: ip-range-expand
description: Expands a CIDR block or start–end IP range into the full address list (or a count) for IPv4 and IPv6.
example_prompt: List all IPs in 192.168.1.0/29
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust big-integer/bit math in WASM; no I/O, runs locally.
rationale: Subnet enumeration is a daily networking task and fully offline-computable.

name: join-lines
description: Joins multiple lines into one using a chosen separator.
example_prompt: join these lines with commas into a single line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: concatenating a line vector with a separator is a pure local transform.
rationale: The inverse of split, needed to turn lists back into a single delimited string for code or queries.

name: json-diff
description: Performs a structural diff of two JSON documents, reporting added, removed and changed keys.
example_prompt: compare these two JSON configs and show only the differences
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses and walks both trees locally.
rationale: A common developer variant of Diff Checker that text diff handles poorly.

name: jsonpath-query
description: Evaluates a JSONPath expression against a JSON document and returns the matched values.
example_prompt: Get $.store.book[*].author from this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json + a pure-Rust JSONPath engine; local eval.
rationale: Extremely common API/data-shaping task that is fully offline-capable.

name: keccak-hash
description: Computes Keccak-256/512 digests (the original Keccak padding used by Ethereum, distinct from FIPS SHA-3).
example_prompt: keccak256 of this contract data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the sha3 crate exposes the legacy Keccak variants in pure Rust, fully offline.
rationale: Keccak-256 is the hash behind every Ethereum address and ABI selector, and is frequently confused with SHA3-256, so a dedicated tool prevents costly mistakes.

name: lz4-compress
description: Compresses input with LZ4 for extremely fast, streaming-friendly compression.
example_prompt: lz4 compress this buffer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust lz4_flex crate — no native deps, runs in the sandbox.
rationale: LZ4 is the default fast-compression codec in databases, games, and logging pipelines, so devs frequently produce it.

name: lz4-decompress
description: Decompresses LZ4 frames or blocks back to raw bytes.
example_prompt: lz4 decompress this block
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via lz4_flex — pure Rust, client-side only.
rationale: Engineers regularly need to peek at LZ4-compressed records emitted by tools like ClickHouse or Kafka.

name: mac-vendor-lookup
description: Resolves the manufacturer of a MAC address from its OUI prefix using a bundled IEEE registry, fully offline.
example_prompt: Who manufactures the device with MAC F0:18:98:11:22:33?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the IEEE OUI/MA-L prefix→vendor table is embedded as a WASM asset so the lookup is a local map query with no API call.
rationale: Identifying device vendors from captured MACs is a daily incident-response and inventory task, and an offline lookup avoids leaking MACs to web services.

name: markdown-to-latex
description: Converts Markdown documents into LaTeX source.
example_prompt: Convert this Markdown into LaTeX
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses Markdown and emits LaTeX with no external tooling.
rationale: Drafting in Markdown then exporting to LaTeX is common for Overleaf/Papeeria users.

name: markdown-to-slides
description: Converts Markdown into a self-contained HTML slide deck.
example_prompt: Make a slide deck from this markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emitting reveal-style HTML; runs fully client-side.
rationale: HackMD's slide mode is a headline feature people actively seek out.

name: math-expression-evaluator
description: Evaluate arithmetic expressions with functions, parentheses and constants.
example_prompt: evaluate (2+3)*sin(pi/2)^2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: an expression-parser crate such as meval, fully local.
rationale: An instant scientific calculator beyond basic operators.

name: md5-hash
description: Computes the MD5 digest of text or a file.
example_prompt: md5 of admin123
