name: candlestick-chart
description: Renders OHLC price data from CSV into a candlestick chart image.
example_prompt: Make a candlestick chart from this OHLC CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (plotters) draws the chart to PNG/SVG entirely in the browser.
rationale: Charting pasted price data mirrors TradingView's core value with no account or upload.

name: carve-files
description: Scans a binary blob for embedded files by magic-byte signatures and extracts the recovered files.
example_prompt: Carve any embedded files out of this memory dump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM signature scan over the uploaded bytes; recovered files are offered as local downloads.
rationale: Maps the CyberChef 'Extract Files' operation; valuable in forensics/CTF and inherently safer offline.

name: chacha20-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the ChaCha20 stream cipher and the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD construction.
example_prompt: Encrypt this text with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and give me the ciphertext and tag in base64
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `chacha20` and `chacha20poly1305` crates; stream-cipher keystream generation is pure compute, fully browser-local.
rationale: ChaCha is the modern TLS-grade stream cipher and a frequent ask for fast authenticated encryption without AES hardware.

name: charset-transcode
description: Re-decodes text or bytes from a legacy charset (ISO-8859-x, Windows-1252, Shift_JIS, etc.) into clean UTF-8, fixing mojibake.
example_prompt: Fix the mojibake in: CafÃ© rÃ©sumÃ©
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: the pure-Rust `encoding_rs` library bundles all WHATWG charset tables, so transcoding runs fully offline.
rationale: Charset mismatches from emails, CSVs, and scraped pages are a frequent source of garbled text, and the encoding tables are too big to do by hand.

name: cidr-calculator
description: Computes network address, broadcast, netmask, wildcard, usable host range, and host count for a CIDR.
example_prompt: What's the network and broadcast for 10.0.5.0/22?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust bit arithmetic in WASM; deterministic and local.
rationale: Subnet calculators are among the most-used networking utilities and require no server.

name: ciphersaber2
description: Encrypts and decrypts data with CipherSaber-2 (RC4 with a random IV and configurable key-setup rounds).
example_prompt: Decrypt this CipherSaber-2 message with passphrase 'secret': <hex blob>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RC4 keystream and IV handling are pure byte math, no host APIs.
rationale: A self-contained teaching cipher with persistent demand that no mainstream tool exposes simply.

name: citation-generator
description: Formats a reference into APA, MLA, or Chicago style from author/title/year fields.
example_prompt: Format this book in APA: author, title, year, publisher.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rule-based templating per style; fully offline.
rationale: Serves Edubirdie's student audience with a legitimate, deterministic academic tool rather than essay-writing.

name: classical-cipher-tool
description: Encrypts and decrypts with Caesar, Vigenère, Atbash, and rail-fence ciphers, including Caesar brute-force.
example_prompt: Decrypt this Vigenère cipher with the key 'lemon'
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM character math; entirely in-memory.
rationale: Cryptii and puzzle/CTF demand centers on classic ciphers that are perfect for local compute.

name: cmac-generate
description: Computes an AES-CMAC (block-cipher MAC) over a message with a 128/192/256-bit key.
example_prompt: Generate the AES-CMAC of this hex message with key 000102...0f
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the cmac + aes crates; block-cipher MACs run entirely in-browser.
rationale: CMAC is common in embedded/IoT and smartcard work where keeping the key off remote servers matters.

name: color-channel-split
description: Splits an image into separate red, green, blue, and alpha channel images for stego and color analysis.
example_prompt: Split this image into its color channels.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; per-channel extraction is a local pixel-wise pass over the decoded image.
rationale: Isolating channels reveals hidden data and is a staple of image forensics.

name: color-contrast-checker
description: Computes the WCAG contrast ratio between two colors and flags AA/AAA pass/fail.
example_prompt: Does white text on #2563EB pass WCAG AA?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; relative-luminance contrast formula, no network.
rationale: Accessibility contrast checks are a frequent dev/design task that's pure math.

name: color-converter
description: Parses a color code (hex, rgb, hsl, or named) and outputs all equivalent formats with a swatch preview.
example_prompt: convert #3498db to rgb and hsl
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; color-space math and SVG swatch generation run locally.
rationale: Designers and developers constantly translate colors between hex, RGB, and HSL.

name: color-shades-generator
description: Produces a ramp of tints, shades and tones for a base color (e.g. a Tailwind-style 50-900 scale).
example_prompt: Generate a 50-900 shade scale for #8B5CF6
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; lightness interpolation in HSL/LAB.
rationale: Building consistent shade scales is a common design-system task captured by the color-tool demand.

name: column-math
description: Performs element-wise add, subtract, multiply, or divide between two equal-length numeric lists/columns.
example_prompt: Multiply each number in column A by the matching number in column B
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — paired float arithmetic over two parsed lists, deterministic and local.
rationale: Row-by-row arithmetic on two columns is a frequent spreadsheet task that this does instantly in chat without opening a spreadsheet.

name: cron-next-runs
description: Computes the next N scheduled fire times for a given cron expression and base time.
example_prompt: when does '0 0 1 * *' next run, list the next 5 times
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schedule iteration over calendar fields is deterministic arithmetic with no network.
rationale: Second distinct tool from crontab-guru demand; engineers often need the actual upcoming run timestamps, not just prose.

name: css-gradient-generator
description: Builds CSS linear/radial gradient code from chosen colors, angle and stops.
example_prompt: Make a CSS linear gradient from #6EE7B7 to #3B82F6 at 45 degrees
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; string/number formatting only.
rationale: Gradient generators are perennially popular with front-end devs and need no server.

name: cumulative-sum
description: Produces the running total (prefix sum) of a list of numbers, with optional running average, min, and max.
example_prompt: Give me the running total of 10, 20, 30, 40
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — single-pass accumulation over parsed numbers, no external runtime.
rationale: Cumulative totals are essential for finance and progress tracking and are awkward to compute by hand on a pasted list.

name: current-time
description: Reports the current date and time in UTC, a chosen timezone, and as a Unix timestamp.
example_prompt: what time is it right now in UTC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formatting over the current epoch the JS host passes from Date.now(); timezone via compiled-in chrono-tz, so no server clock is contacted.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Get Time' demand and anchors all the relative date tools in one place.

name: data-uri-encode
description: Builds a data: URI from text or pasted bytes with a chosen MIME type and base64 or percent encoding.
example_prompt: Make a data URI for this SVG with image/svg+xml
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: prepend the MIME header and base64/percent-encode the payload, no network.
rationale: Inlining small assets as data URIs is a common front-end optimization that's tedious to do by hand.

name: disposable-email-detector
description: Flags whether an email address uses a known disposable or throwaway-inbox domain.
example_prompt: Is test@mailinator.com a disposable email?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lookup against an embedded list of disposable domains; offline.
rationale: Turns Mailinator demand into the defensive flip side — detecting throwaway inboxes — which embeds a static list locally.

name: dns-message-parser
description: Parses a DNS wire-format message (hex or base64url) into header flags, questions, and resource records, decoding name compression.
example_prompt: Parse this DNS response packet (hex): 1234818000010001...
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust DNS parser with compression-pointer support in WASM; no network needed.
rationale: Reading raw DNS packets (including DoH wire-format responses) is hard by hand and fully offline-doable.

name: drop-bytes
description: Removes the first or last N bytes or characters from text.
example_prompt: drop the first 4 characters from each of these lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: byte/char slicing is a pure in-memory operation with no external calls.
rationale: Trimming fixed-length prefixes/suffixes (timestamps, markers) is a precise cleanup users repeatedly need.

name: elf-info
description: Parses an ELF binary and reports its header, architecture, sections, segments, and symbol table.
example_prompt: Show me the ELF header and sections of this binary.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust goblin/object crate; parsing is pure byte decoding.
rationale: Quick offline triage of Linux binaries without shelling out to readelf.

name: email-obfuscator
description: Encodes an email address into scraper-resistant HTML-entity, JavaScript, and CSS-reversed variants you can paste into a page.
example_prompt: Obfuscate my email joris@suppers.ai so bots can't scrape it
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM — pure string transformation (entity/JS/CSS encoding) with no network, runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: scr.im's whole value is hiding an email from harvesters, which is pure local text encoding with no server dependency.

name: emoji-search
description: Searches emoji by keyword, shortcode, or category and returns the matching glyphs.
example_prompt: find emoji for celebration and party
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lookup over an embedded Unicode emoji keyword dataset, no network.
rationale: Direct match for Emoji Search Online and the small dataset bundles cleanly into WASM.

name: equation-solver
description: Solves algebraic equations and simplifies symbolic expressions step by step.
example_prompt: Solve 2x^2 - 8x + 6 = 0
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs SymPy in the Python sandbox for exact symbolic math locally.
rationale: Symbolic math serves heavy Study-and-Education demand with no compute backend.

name: evp-derive
description: Reproduces OpenSSL's legacy EVP_BytesToKey key/IV derivation from a password, salt, and hash.
example_prompt: Derive the AES-256-CBC key and IV OpenSSL would use for password 'pass', salt 0x0102030405060708
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — iterative MD5/SHA digesting is pure byte math, no system OpenSSL needed.
rationale: Essential for decrypting legacy `openssl enc` blobs, a recurring real-world pain point.

name: extract-hashes
description: Extracts hex hash strings (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512) from text, grouped by detected algorithm.
example_prompt: Grab all the SHA-256 hashes out of this IOC list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM length/charset regex; pure text processing offline.
rationale: Core step in malware-IOC workflows where analysts pull hashes from reports to check elsewhere.

name: extract-mac-addresses
description: Extracts MAC addresses from text in any common notation and normalizes them to a single format.
example_prompt: Find all the MAC addresses in this DHCP log and normalize them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex + reformat; fully offline.
rationale: Network/forensics audiences need this and the input is often confidential infrastructure data.

name: extract-rgba
description: Decodes an image and exports its raw per-pixel RGBA values as text, CSV, or JSON for inspection or scripting.
example_prompt: Give me the raw RGBA pixel values of this image.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with the image crate; decoding to a raw pixel buffer is pure local computation.
rationale: Useful for debugging graphics, sampling colors, and feeding pixel data into other analysis.

name: extract-video-metadata
description: Reports container, codecs, resolution, frame rate, duration, bitrate and stream list for a video (ffprobe-style).
example_prompt: What codec and resolution is this mp4?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (ffmpeg.wasm) demuxes the container in-browser to read stream info; large files never upload.
rationale: Extends the metadata family to video and reuses the already-available ffmpeg loader.

name: favicon-generator
description: Generates a multi-size favicon bundle (ICO plus 16–512px PNGs and a web manifest) from one image.
example_prompt: Make a favicon set from this logo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the image crate resizes and the ico crate packs the bundle, no server needed.
rationale: favicon-generator is a high-traffic dev utility that maps cleanly to local image resizing.

name: file-tree-generator
description: Turns a list of file paths or indented outline into an ASCII tree diagram for READMEs and docs.
example_prompt: make a file tree from these paths: src/main.rs, src/lib.rs, tests/it.rs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; path grouping and tree rendering run in-browser.
rationale: Generating tidy directory-tree diagrams is a common documentation need.

name: flask-session-decode
description: Decodes a Flask/itsdangerous session cookie into readable JSON without the secret key, handling base64url, optional zlib compression, and timestamp parsing.
example_prompt: Decode this Flask session cookie: eyJ1c2VyIjoxfQ.aBcDeF.gHiJkL...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decoding is base64url + zlib inflate + JSON parse, all available as pure-Rust crates compiled to WASM with no signature needed.
rationale: Inspecting Flask session contents is a constant developer/debugging need and runs safely client-side so cookies never leave the browser.

name: font-identifier
description: Identifies the most likely font(s) from an uploaded image of text.
example_prompt: what font is used in this screenshot?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a font-classification vision model on the decoded image entirely in-browser.
rationale: WhatTheFont is high-demand and currently requires uploading images to a third party.

name: function-grapher
description: Plots one or more y=f(x) functions over a range and returns an SVG graph with axes and gridlines.
example_prompt: graph y = sin(x) and y = x/2 from -10 to 10
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates the expression and emits an SVG plot string; no canvas or network needed.
rationale: Brings Desmos-style graphing into chat as a shareable SVG, fully browser-local.

name: fuzzy-hash-compare
description: Compares two SSDEEP/CTPH hashes and returns a 0–100 similarity score indicating how alike the original inputs are.
example_prompt: how similar are these two ssdeep hashes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the SSDEEP comparison is a pure edit-distance computation over the two fingerprint strings, fully offline.
rationale: Generating a fuzzy hash is only useful if you can score similarity, so the compare step completes the CTPH workflow for malware triage and dedup.

name: generate-uuid
description: Generates UUIDs in v4 (random), v7 (time-ordered), v1, or v5/v3 (namespace) form, singly or in bulk.
example_prompt: generate a v7 uuid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `uuid` crate with browser RNG via the host produces all versions offline
rationale: UUID generation is an extremely common developer need and works perfectly as a zero-latency local tool.

name: geometry-calculator
description: Calculates area, perimeter, surface area, and volume for common 2D and 3D shapes from their dimensions.
example_prompt: surface area and volume of a cylinder radius 3 height 10
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formula evaluation, deterministic and browser-local.
rationale: Direct match for the MathIsFun geometry-sheet demand as an interactive calculator.

name: gost-kuznyechik-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the GOST R 34.12-2015 Kuznyechik 128-bit block cipher.
example_prompt: Encrypt 'секрет' with GOST Kuznyechik using this 256-bit key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the RustCrypto `kuznyechik` crate — deterministic CPU-only computation, fully client-side.
rationale: Kuznyechik is the modern GOST block-cipher standard and complements Magma for full GOST decrypt coverage.

name: gost-magma-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the GOST 28147-89 / Magma block cipher in ECB or CBC mode.
example_prompt: Decrypt this GOST Magma ciphertext with this 256-bit key
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `magma`/`gost` RustCrypto crates; deterministic rounds run in wasmi.
rationale: GOST is the Russian government standard frequently encountered in CTFs and regional interop.

name: gradient-image-generator
description: Creates a solid, linear- or radial-gradient image at a chosen size for backgrounds and placeholders.
example_prompt: Generate a 1920x1080 blue-to-purple gradient
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fills a pixel buffer procedurally, no model needed.
rationale: Instant backgrounds and placeholder assets are a steady design need.

name: graph-algorithms
description: Runs BFS, DFS, shortest path, topological sort and cycle detection on a user-supplied graph.
example_prompt: find the shortest path from A to F in this graph: A-B 2, B-F 5, A-C 1, C-F 3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements the algorithms in-process; purely computational.
rationale: Directly serves the directed-graph-editor crowd who need answers, not just a picture.

name: hash-all
description: Generates every common digest (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA3-256, RIPEMD-160, BLAKE2, BLAKE3, Whirlpool) for the same text or file at once in a labeled table.
example_prompt: generate all hashes for "correct horse battery staple"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — all algorithms are pure-Rust crates run sequentially over the same input buffer, fully offline in wasmi.
rationale: Directly answers the high-demand 'generate all hashes / generate all checksums' query in a single pass instead of forcing repeated single-algorithm runs.

name: head-lines
description: Outputs the first N lines of text.
example_prompt: show me the first 10 lines of this
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: taking the first N elements of a line vector is pure in-memory work.
rationale: Quickly previewing the top of a large paste mirrors the ubiquitous `head` command.

name: hex-codec
description: Encodes text or bytes to a hexadecimal string and decodes hex back to text, with optional byte delimiters.
example_prompt: convert "Hello" to hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte-to-nibble mapping is pure computation, no network or filesystem needed.
rationale: Hex encode/decode is one of the most-searched developer conversions and pairs naturally with the base64 demand.

name: hex-to-pem
description: Wraps DER hex bytes back into PEM format with a chosen label and 64-char line folding.
example_prompt: wrap this DER hex into a PEM certificate block
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hex decode, base64 encode, and line wrapping, all in-memory
rationale: Reconstructing PEM from raw bytes is a recurring need for tooling that only outputs DER, and it's privacy-sensitive.

name: hexbin-density-chart
description: Plots a hexagonal-bin density heatmap from x/y point data and renders it as SVG or PNG.
example_prompt: Make a hexbin density chart from this list of coordinates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bins points and emits SVG; pyodide+matplotlib optional — both run locally.
rationale: Hexbin plots reveal density in large scatter data where plain points overplot.

name: hkdf-derive
description: Performs HKDF extract-and-expand key derivation with configurable hash, salt, info, and length.
example_prompt: Run HKDF-SHA256 with IKM 0x0b0b..., salt 0x000102, info 'app', output 42 bytes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RustCrypto hkdf crate computes deterministically on-device.
rationale: Widely used in modern protocols; engineers want a quick, private way to verify expected outputs.

name: html-form-generator
description: Generates accessible HTML form markup with labeled inputs, validation attributes, and basic styling from a plain description of fields.
example_prompt: build a contact form with name, email, message and a submit button
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating from parsed field list, browser-local.
rationale: Direct match for pForm's form-builder demand without a hosted designer.

name: http-header-analyzer
description: Parses pasted HTTP response headers and explains caching, compression, server hints, and missing security headers.
example_prompt: Analyze these response headers and tell me what security headers I'm missing: <pasted headers>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of pasted header text; fully deterministic and offline.
rationale: Turns the WhoIsHostingThis inspection intent into a concrete dev win — header auditing is a frequent, browser-local-friendly task.

name: image-to-ascii
description: Converts an image into ASCII or ANSI character art.
example_prompt: Turn this logo into ASCII art
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM samples luminance and maps to a glyph ramp locally.
rationale: Fun, shareable Graphics/Text crossover with steady novelty demand.

name: image-to-ico
description: Generates a multi-resolution .ico favicon from a PNG or JPG source image.
example_prompt: make a favicon.ico from this logo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (image/ico crates): resize + ICO encoding are pure-Rust codecs running client-side.
rationale: Favicon generation is a perennial web-dev need that pairs well with the image-conversion suite.

name: image-to-pixel-art
description: Converts an image into limited-palette pixel art.
example_prompt: Make this photo into pixel art
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (image) downscale plus palette quantization.
rationale: Directly serves Piskel/PixelCraft pixel-art demand.

name: ip-range-to-cidr
description: Converts an arbitrary start–end IP range into the minimal set of CIDR blocks that exactly covers it.
example_prompt: Convert the range 192.168.1.5 to 192.168.1.30 into CIDR blocks
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust greedy bit-alignment algorithm in WASM; runs in-browser.
rationale: Range-to-CIDR aggregation is needed for firewall/ACL rules and is awkward to do by hand.

name: ja3-fingerprint
description: Computes the JA3 TLS client fingerprint string and its MD5 hash from a raw ClientHello.
example_prompt: Give me the JA3 fingerprint of this ClientHello: 16030100c2010000be0303...
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust ClientHello parse plus an MD5 crate in WASM; no network.
rationale: JA3 is a standard for client fingerprinting in threat hunting and is computable entirely offline.

name: ja4-server-fingerprint
description: Computes the JA4S server fingerprint from a raw ServerHello.
example_prompt: Compute the JA4S fingerprint for this ServerHello: 1603030051020000...
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust ServerHello parse plus SHA-256 in WASM; deterministic and local.
rationale: JA4S completes the modern JA4 fingerprint suite for server identification.

name: js-beautify
description: Re-indents and formats obfuscated or minified JavaScript into readable source.
example_prompt: beautify this minified JS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the swc parser + code printer, both WASM-compatible; local AST round-trip.
rationale: Un-minifying JS to inspect bundled or vendor code is a very common reverse-engineering need.

name: js-minify
description: Minifies JavaScript by shortening names and stripping whitespace while preserving behavior.
example_prompt: minify this JavaScript
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via swc's minifier compiled to WASM; deterministic client-side transform.
rationale: Quick JS minification without a Node toolchain is genuinely useful for snippets and demos.

name: json-ld-generator
description: Generates schema.org JSON-LD markup (Article, Product, FAQ, and more) from simple field inputs.
example_prompt: Generate JSON-LD Product schema for a $20 blue mug
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM — building JSON-LD is pure local templating and serialization.
rationale: Pairs with the structured-data demand by producing valid markup locally, a common SEO need.

name: jsonata-query
description: Evaluates a JSONata query/transform expression against a JSON document.
example_prompt: Use JSONata to sum order.items.(price*qty) in this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust jsonata engine; runs entirely on the pasted JSON.
rationale: JSONata is the go-to transform language in low-code/integration tooling and lacks a good offline playground.

name: jwt-decode
description: Decodes a JWT into readable header and payload JSON without verifying the signature, flagging expiry and standard claims.
example_prompt: Decode this JWT and show me the claims: eyJhbGciOi...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — base64url decode plus JSON parsing, entirely offline so tokens never leave the device.
rationale: Inspecting tokens is the single most common JWT task, and doing it privately is a major privacy win.

name: krutidev-unicode-converter
description: Converts legacy Kruti Dev Hindi text to Unicode Devanagari and back.
example_prompt: Convert this Kruti Dev text to Unicode Hindi: <text>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM glyph-remapping table (deterministic character mapping both directions); no network.
rationale: A high-demand need for a large Hindi-typing audience that is purely a character mapping — ideal browser-local fit.

name: latex-equation-render
description: Renders a LaTeX math expression to a crisp PNG or SVG image.
example_prompt: Render \int_0^1 x^2 dx as an image
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs matplotlib's mathtext to rasterize the equation locally.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Latex' demand for equation images in slides and docs.

name: latex-table
description: Converts CSV or TSV data into a LaTeX tabular environment.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into a LaTeX table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the rows and emits LaTeX markup locally.
rationale: Building tables is the most tedious part of Overleaf/Papeeria writing and is pure text generation.

name: latex-to-mathml
description: Converts LaTeX math expressions into rendered MathML for display and reuse.
example_prompt: render this formula: \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM translates LaTeX to MathML which the browser renders natively.
rationale: KeepFormula demand shows people want to store and render math formulas quickly and locally.

name: lrc-timing-shifter
description: Offsets every timestamp in an LRC lyric file by a number of milliseconds to re-sync it.
example_prompt: Shift this LRC file 500ms earlier
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic over the parsed timestamps; fully local.
rationale: Synced lyrics are almost always slightly off and a one-shot offset is the standard fix.

name: luhn-checkdigit
description: Computes the Luhn check digit that makes a partial number valid.
example_prompt: What Luhn check digit completes 453957876362148?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; deriving the check digit is local mod-10 arithmetic.
rationale: Generating valid test card/IMEI numbers is a common QA need with no server dependency.

name: lz-string-compress
description: Compresses a string with LZString into UTF-16, Base64, or URI-safe form for compact URLs and localStorage.
example_prompt: lz-string compress this JSON so I can put it in a URL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via a Rust lz-string port — pure string math, runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: LZString is the de-facto way web apps pack state into URLs and localStorage, so a local encoder is a frequent dev need.

name: lznt1-decompress
description: Decompresses LZNT1 blobs produced by Windows RtlCompressBuffer (registry hives, hibernation files, malware configs).
example_prompt: decompress this lznt1 hex dump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — LZNT1 is a small LZ77 variant reimplemented in pure Rust, runs in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: LZNT1 shows up constantly in Windows forensics and CTF work and there is no clean browser-local decoder for it.

name: mac-address-format
description: Reformats one or many MAC addresses between colon, hyphen, Cisco dotted, and bare styles with chosen upper/lower case.
example_prompt: Reformat 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E into Cisco dotted notation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure normalization of hex octets and delimiter substitution; no external data needed.
rationale: Network engineers constantly convert MACs between vendor-specific notations and this is a tiny, high-frequency utility.

name: macd-calculator
description: Computes the MACD line, signal line and histogram from prices.
example_prompt: Give me the MACD for this price series
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives the EMAs and MACD locally.
rationale: MACD is a widely-used momentum indicator and is pure deterministic math.

name: magnet-link-parser
description: Decodes a magnet URI into its info-hash, display name, and tracker list, and rebuilds magnet links from parts.
example_prompt: What's the info hash and trackers in this magnet link?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM string/URL parsing; pure text transform with no I/O.
rationale: Magnet links are opaque strings the seedbox crowd needs to read and edit, and nothing does it locally.

name: markdown-section-extractor
description: Extracts a single subsection from a Markdown document by its heading.
example_prompt: Pull just the 'Installation' section out of this README
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM heading parser walks the AST; pure text processing, browser-local.
rationale: Grabbing one part of a long doc is a common need that beats manual scrolling and copy-paste.

name: morse-code
description: Converts text to Morse code and Morse code back to text.
example_prompt: Translate 'SOS help' to Morse code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lookup-table mapping in both directions, runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Covers both To and From Morse Code; a perennial utility request.

name: nt-hash
description: Computes the NT (NTLM) hash of a password by MD4-hashing its UTF-16LE encoding.
example_prompt: What's the NT hash of 'Password1'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the md4 crate; UTF-16LE encoding plus MD4 is deterministic local math.
rationale: Pentesters and AD admins frequently need NT hashes for pass-the-hash and cracking workflows, offline.

name: opml-converter
description: Converts OPML subscription files (podcast/RSS exports) to and from JSON and CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this OPML subscription export into CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM XML/CSV transform; entirely local on the uploaded file.
rationale: OPML is the universal podcast/feed export format and migrating between apps needs format conversion.

name: outline-to-mindmap
description: Turns an indented text outline into a mind-map SVG.
example_prompt: Make a mind map from this outline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tree layout emitting SVG.
rationale: Maps the bubbl mind-mapping demand into a fast text-driven generator.

name: page-weight-analyzer
description: Parses pasted HTML and reports resource counts, inline/render-blocking script and stylesheet tags, and an estimated page-weight budget.
example_prompt: analyze the performance of this page: <paste full HTML source>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML tokenizer; works on pasted markup with no network, so no CORS/server fetch needed for the live site.
rationale: Captures GTmetrix/DebugBear demand for page-speed insight without the server-side crawl those services require.

name: parse-grpc-frame
description: Parses gRPC length-prefixed message framing (compression flag + 4-byte length) and decodes each embedded protobuf payload field tree.
example_prompt: Parse this gRPC frame: 00000000 12 089601120c...
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust framing parser reusing the protobuf walker in WASM; runs locally.
rationale: gRPC payloads captured from the wire are opaque until the framing and protobuf are decoded together.

name: parse-websocket-frame
description: Decodes a WebSocket frame into FIN/RSV/opcode, mask flag, payload length, and the unmasked payload bytes.
example_prompt: Parse this WebSocket frame: 818bff34 ...
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust frame parser with XOR unmasking in WASM; runs in-browser.
rationale: Reading and unmasking raw WebSocket frames from captures is otherwise manual and error-prone.

name: pem-to-hex
description: Strips PEM armor, base64-decodes the body, and emits the underlying DER bytes as hex.
example_prompt: convert this PEM certificate to hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — base64 decode plus hex encode, no crypto/network required
rationale: Cert and key inspection workflows need raw DER hex, and keys must never leave the browser.

name: percentage-calculator
description: Compute percentages, percent change and percent-of-total in one place.
example_prompt: what is 15% of 240 and what percent is 30 of 240
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure arithmetic.
rationale: Ubiquitous quick-math request that fits perfectly in chat.

name: pgp-key-info
description: Parses an armored OpenPGP key and shows its fingerprint, key ID, algorithm, creation/expiry, user IDs, and subkeys.
example_prompt: Show me the details of this PGP public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via rpgp packet parsing; a read-only local inspection with no network.
rationale: Inspecting a PGP key's fingerprint and capabilities is a frequent trust-verification step lacking a quick web tool.

name: phone-parser-formatter
description: Parses a phone number and formats it as E.164, international, and national, reporting region and validity.
example_prompt: parse and format +1 (415) 555-2671
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the phonenumber crate with its embedded metadata; fully offline.
rationale: Phone normalization is a frequent data-cleaning need that benefits from running on private contact data locally.

name: photo-filter-presets
description: Applies named photo filters (sepia, vintage, warm, cool, noir) to an image.
example_prompt: Give this a vintage sepia filter
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies the colour-matrix/LUT per pixel locally.
rationale: One-tap aesthetic filters are a familiar, high-engagement feature.

name: playlist-converter
description: Parses and converts internet-radio and music playlists between M3U/M3U8, PLS, and JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this M3U radio playlist into a PLS file
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM text parser; pure format conversion with no streaming.
rationale: Internet Radio / Jango / Radio Garden listeners shuffle station playlists between players that demand different formats.

name: plist-viewer
description: Parses Apple property lists (both XML and binary bplist) and renders them as readable JSON or a key/value tree.
example_prompt: parse this binary plist and show me the keys
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `plist` crate decodes XML and binary formats with no system dependency
rationale: Binary plists are opaque without tooling, and a local viewer is valuable for macOS/iOS forensics and config inspection.

name: podcast-feed-parser
description: Parses a pasted podcast RSS/XML feed into a clean episode list with titles, dates, durations, and audio URLs.
example_prompt: Parse this podcast RSS feed into a list of episodes
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM XML parser; works on the pasted feed text, no fetching.
rationale: Podbay-style users want a quick episode breakdown of a feed without loading a heavyweight player.

name: python-trace-visualizer
description: Runs Python line by line and returns a step-by-step trace of variable values and the call stack at each step.
example_prompt: Show me a step-by-step execution trace of this Python function
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs CPython in WASM and sys.settrace captures per-line variable state locally, reproducing PythonTutor with no server.
rationale: PythonTutor's step-through visualization is a popular learning aid that maps directly onto pyodide's in-browser tracing.

name: randomize-palette
description: Randomly remaps the color palette of an indexed GIF/PNG-8 image to expose hidden shapes and stego payloads.
example_prompt: Randomize the color palette of this GIF.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; palette remapping operates entirely on the local indexed-image data.
rationale: Palette shuffling instantly reveals data hidden in near-identical palette entries.

name: rc2-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with RC2 at a configurable effective key length in ECB or CBC mode.
example_prompt: Decrypt this RC2-CBC blob with a 40-bit effective key and this IV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `rc2` crate; block transforms are pure compute with no I/O.
rationale: RC2 appears in old S/MIME and PKCS#12 files, so reading legacy certificate exports needs it.

name: rc6-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the RC6 block cipher in ECB or CBC mode.
example_prompt: Decrypt this RC6 ciphertext with a 256-bit key and this IV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via an RC6 implementation over the RustCrypto `cipher` traits; data-dependent rotations are pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: RC6 was an AES finalist still used in research and CTFs, with little tooling available.

name: regex-tester
description: Tests a regular expression against input, showing all matches and named/numbered capture groups.
example_prompt: test the regex \d{3}-\d{4} against these phone numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the regex crate; evaluation is fully client-side.
rationale: Developers constantly need to validate and debug regex patterns against sample data.

name: remove-control-chars
description: Strips null bytes and non-printable control characters from text.
example_prompt: remove the null bytes and control characters from this string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: filtering by Unicode category is a pure in-memory pass with no I/O.
rationale: Covers the 'Remove null bytes' demand and fixes corrupted/binary-tainted pastes that break downstream tools.

name: ripemd160-hash
description: Computes the RIPEMD-160 digest of text or a file.
example_prompt: ripemd160 of this public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the ripemd RustCrypto crate is pure-Rust and deterministic in wasmi.
rationale: RIPEMD-160 is a core step in Bitcoin address generation, giving it durable niche demand from crypto developers.

name: risk-matrix
description: Plots likelihood-versus-impact items onto a colored risk matrix heatmap with green/amber/red zones.
example_prompt: Create a 5x5 risk matrix heatmap for these project risks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM positions items on a fixed grid and emits an SVG with zone coloring — no external dependencies.
rationale: Risk matrices are ubiquitous in project and security planning and map naturally onto the heatmap primitive.

name: rsa-encrypt
description: Encrypts a small payload to an RSA public key using OAEP or PKCS#1 v1.5 padding, returning base64 ciphertext.
example_prompt: RSA-encrypt this text with this public key using OAEP
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the rsa crate; encryption runs client-side with no plaintext egress.
rationale: Encrypting a secret to someone's RSA key (e.g. a config value) is a common need best done where the plaintext stays local.

name: rsi-calculator
description: Computes the Relative Strength Index from a price series.
example_prompt: Calculate the 14-period RSI for these closing prices
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes RSI from pasted data with no external feed.
rationale: RSI is a staple TradingView indicator traders want to compute on their own data.

name: seconds-to-hms
description: Converts a number of seconds into HH:MM:SS (or D:HH:MM:SS) clock format.
example_prompt: convert 5025 seconds to time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — divmod arithmetic and formatting run entirely in the sandbox.
rationale: Exact match for the convert-seconds-to-time demand, common for video/duration handling.

name: seo-audit
description: Audits pasted HTML for SEO issues — missing title/meta description, heading hierarchy, image alt text, canonical, and Open Graph tags — and scores them.
example_prompt: run an SEO audit on this page: <paste HTML>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parsing and rule checks, no network calls required.
rationale: Reproduces WooRank's on-page checklist locally and privately, the part that doesn't need backlink crawling.

name: sha3-hash
description: Computes SHA3-256/384/512 (FIPS 202) digests of text or a file.
example_prompt: sha3-256 hash of this data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the sha3 RustCrypto crate implements the Keccak sponge in pure Rust, running deterministically in wasmi.
rationale: SHA-3 is the current NIST standard and distinct enough from SHA-2 to deserve its own tool for developers adopting it.

name: slugify
description: Converts a title or phrase into a clean URL-safe slug: lowercased, transliterated to ASCII, with spaces and punctuation collapsed to hyphens.
example_prompt: make a url slug from: Crème Brûlée — The Best Recipe!
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: combines ASCII transliteration with hyphenation/collapse logic, no network needed.
rationale: Slug generation is a constant need for blogs, CMS entries and filenames and builds directly on the diacritic/transliteration work.

name: sm2-keypair-generate
description: Generates a fresh SM2 (GM/T 0003) key pair, returning the private scalar and public point in hex and PEM.
example_prompt: Generate an SM2 key pair for me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2`; uses the host secure-random import (or a user-supplied entropy seed) for the scalar, otherwise pure compute in wasmi.
rationale: Every SM2 encrypt/sign workflow starts with a keypair, and generating Chinese-standard keys locally avoids trusting a remote service with the private key.

name: sm2-public-from-private
description: Derives the SM2 public key point from an SM2 private key scalar, output as uncompressed/compressed hex or PEM.
example_prompt: Derive the SM2 public key from this private key: 0x3945208f...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2`; a single deterministic scalar×G multiplication with no randomness or network, runs in wasmi.
rationale: Sits squarely at the intersection of both demand themes (public-from-private + SM2) and is the first step in any ShangMi key workflow.

name: sm4-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the SM4 block cipher in ECB or CBC mode.
example_prompt: Encrypt this text with SM4-CBC using key and IV in hex
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `sm4` + `cbc` crates; pure block-cipher rounds, fully browser-local.
rationale: SM4 is China's mandated commercial cipher, so interop with Chinese systems is a recurring demand.

name: smart-quotes-clean
description: Replaces smart quotes, em/en dashes, ellipses, and other typographic characters with plain ASCII equivalents.
example_prompt: replace the smart quotes in: “hello” — it’s nice…
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a fixed character-substitution map applied in-memory.
rationale: Cleaning Word/Docs-pasted text of curly quotes is a frequent real annoyance for code, CSVs, and CLI input.

name: spritesheet-slice
description: Slices a grid sprite sheet into individual frame PNGs.
example_prompt: Slice this 4x4 sprite sheet into separate PNGs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (image) grid cropping.
rationale: Common Piskel/game-asset chore done locally with no upload.

name: spritesheet-to-gif
description: Combines sprite frames into an animated GIF.
example_prompt: Animate these sprite frames into a GIF
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM stitching frames into a GIF, client-side.
rationale: GIF export is Piskel's core sprite-animation workflow.

name: sql-beautify
description: Formats SQL queries with consistent keyword casing, indentation, and clause line breaks.
example_prompt: format this SQL query
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the sqlformat crate; pure string transform, no DB connection.
rationale: Readable SQL formatting is a daily need for analysts and backend developers.

name: strip-ansi-codes
description: Removes ANSI escape and color codes from terminal output.
example_prompt: strip the color codes out of this terminal log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ANSI sequences are matched and stripped with a pure-Rust scanner, no runtime dependencies.
rationale: Pasting colorized CI/terminal logs is common and the raw escape codes make text unreadable until stripped.

name: structured-data-validator
description: Extracts and validates JSON-LD, microdata, and RDFa structured data from pasted HTML and flags schema.org errors.
example_prompt: Check the structured data / schema.org markup in this HTML
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM — HTML/JSON parsing and schema validation are pure local computation, replacing Google's hosted testing tool.
rationale: Google's Structured Data Testing Tool was widely used for SEO, and the parse-and-validate step needs no server.

name: subtitle-merge
description: Merges or combines multiple SRT/VTT subtitle files with optional time-shift.
example_prompt: Combine these two SRT subtitle files and shift the second by 3 seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SRT/VTT parser and timestamp math; browser-local.
rationale: Bilingual or split-recording subtitles often need merging/realigning, and it's painful to do manually.

name: svg-placeholder-generator
description: Generate a placeholder SVG image at a given size with optional label text.
example_prompt: make a 600x400 placeholder svg labeled 'hero'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: string templating into an SVG, no network.
rationale: Instant mockup asset with zero external image-service dependency.

name: tail-lines
description: Outputs the last N lines of text.
example_prompt: give me just the last 20 lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: slicing the tail of a line vector is a pure local operation.
rationale: Inspecting the end of logs/output is a constant need and matches the familiar `tail` command.

name: temperature-converter
description: Convert temperatures between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin.
example_prompt: convert 98.6F to celsius
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: affine arithmetic only.
rationale: Everyday conversion that belongs in a quick-tools chat.

name: text-banner-image
description: Renders stylized text (font, colors, outline, shadow, gradient fill) to a PNG banner.
example_prompt: Make a glowing red 'GAME OVER' banner PNG with a black outline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; rasterize glyphs with `ab_glyph`/`cosmic-text` and a bundled font set.
rationale: Directly maps to FlamingText-style styled-text graphics and is fully expressible as local glyph rasterization.

name: text-diff
description: Compares two blocks of text and highlights added, removed, and changed lines.
example_prompt: diff these two versions of my config and show me what changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a line-level LCS/Myers diff is pure string and array work with no I/O, so it runs entirely in the wasmi runtime client-side.
rationale: Diffing pasted text is one of the most-searched developer utilities and there is no privacy-safe browser-local option in a chat.

name: text-to-table
description: Renders delimited text (CSV/TSV) as an aligned ASCII or Markdown table.
example_prompt: turn this CSV into a markdown table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing delimiters and computing column widths is pure in-memory work with no server round-trip.
rationale: Converting raw delimited data into a readable/pasteable table is a high-demand formatting task.

name: text-to-unicode
description: Lists each character's Unicode code point, name and escape sequence (\u / U+) for the given text.
example_prompt: show the unicode code points for café 🚀
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — iterates chars with a bundled Unicode name table; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Debugging mojibake, hidden characters and emoji needs a quick code-point inspector without sending text to a web service.

name: time-to-decimal-hours
description: Converts an HH:MM clock duration into decimal hours (e.g. 1:30 → 1.5) and back.
example_prompt: convert 7:45 to decimal hours
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — minutes/60 arithmetic and rounding are pure math done client-side.
rationale: Maps the convert-time-to-decimal demand, a staple of timesheet and payroll calculations.

name: toc-generator
description: Builds a linked table of contents from the headings of a Markdown or HTML document.
example_prompt: Generate a table of contents for this Markdown file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans headings and slugifies anchors; no rendering engine or server needed.
rationale: TOCs are expected in long docs and wikis, and automating them keeps anchors consistent.

name: truncate-text
description: Shortens text to a chosen number of characters or words, appending an ellipsis.
example_prompt: truncate this to 100 characters with a …
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with Unicode-aware char counting; no model or network
rationale: Producing previews/excerpts at an exact length is a frequent copywriting need.

name: unicode-to-text
description: Decodes \uXXXX, U+XXXX and HTML numeric escape sequences back into readable text.
example_prompt: decode \u0063\u0061\u0066\u00e9 to text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure parsing of escape tokens into chars, runs entirely in the sandbox.
rationale: The inverse of escaping is just as commonly needed when reading logs, JSON or scraped data.

name: unix-timestamp-converter
description: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates in any format.
example_prompt: convert 1718750000 to a readable date
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: chrono formatting, no backend.
rationale: Daily dev and ops need that should never require a round-trip.

name: url-codec
description: Percent-encodes and decodes URLs and query-string components, including form (+) handling.
example_prompt: url-decode hello%20world%26foo%3Dbar
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — percent-encoding is a byte-level transform with no network access.
rationale: URL encode/decode is among the most-searched developer utilities and is constantly needed for debugging links and APIs.

name: waveform-image
description: Renders a static waveform image from an audio file.
example_prompt: Make a waveform PNG of this song
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg showwavespic generates the image entirely client-side.
rationale: Waveform thumbnails are wanted for posts and players and are a one-shot ffmpeg render.

name: xml-beautify
description: Reformats XML with consistent indentation and line breaks while preserving attributes and CDATA.
example_prompt: format this XML nicely
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via quick-xml event reader/writer; deterministic local reformatting.
rationale: XML/SOAP/config files remain widespread and are painful to read unformatted.

name: xor-cipher
description: XORs text or hex data against a repeating key and outputs hex, Base64 or UTF-8.
example_prompt: XOR 'hello' with key 'cafe' and show the result in hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte-wise XOR with simple encoding, no network or native deps.
rationale: A foundational obfuscation/crypto primitive used constantly in CTFs and quick data masking.

name: xpath-query
description: Runs an XPath 1.0 expression against an XML or XHTML document and returns matching nodes or values.
example_prompt: Run //book/title on this XML and give me the titles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via sxd-document + sxd-xpath (pure Rust, no libxml); parses in-browser.
rationale: Developers constantly test XPath against private data and want it without a server or browser console.

name: xsalsa20-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with XSalsa20 using an extended 192-bit (24-byte) nonce.
example_prompt: Decrypt this XSalsa20 ciphertext with this key and 24-byte nonce
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the `salsa20` crate's XSalsa20 variant; pure keystream compute, browser-local.
rationale: XSalsa20 underpins NaCl/libsodium secretbox, so it's needed to interoperate with sodium-encrypted payloads.

name: yaml-to-toml
description: Converts a YAML document into equivalent TOML.
example_prompt: convert this yaml config to toml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — serde_yaml parse then toml serialization, fully in-memory.
rationale: Moving config between ecosystems (e.g. into Rust/Cargo-style TOML) is awkward by hand and ideal for automation.

name: z-score-normalize
description: Standardizes a list of numbers to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 (z-scores), or min-max scales to 0–1.
example_prompt: Normalize these numbers to z-scores: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — computes mean/std then transforms each value, fully local arithmetic.
rationale: Feature scaling is a routine ML/data-prep step that maps the mean and standard-deviation demand into a directly useful transform.

name: zero-width-cleaner
description: Detects and strips invisible zero-width spaces, joiners, BOMs and other non-printing characters from pasted text.
example_prompt: clean the invisible characters out of this pasted text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: filters a known set of zero-width/format codepoints, no dependencies, fully offline.
rationale: Pasted text frequently carries hidden characters that break diffs, search and tokenization; cleaning them is a real everyday need.

name: add-line-numbers
description: Prefixes every line with a sequential line number.
example_prompt: add line numbers to this code snippet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: splitting on newlines and prepending counters is pure string work in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Numbered lines are frequently needed for referencing code/log lines in discussions.

name: app-icon-set
description: Produces a full PWA/iOS/Android app-icon set at all required sizes from a single source image.
example_prompt: Generate all the app icon sizes from this image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure image-crate downscaling to a fixed size matrix runs client-side.
rationale: Devs constantly regenerate icon sets and the favicon-generator demand extends naturally to full app icons.

name: asn1-parser
description: Parses an ASN.1/DER hex string into a readable tree of tags, lengths, OIDs, and decoded primitive values.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive TLV/DER walker over the hex bytes, no external services
rationale: Inspecting certificate and key structures is hard without a parser, and uploading private material to a web ASN.1 decoder is a real risk this avoids.

name: audio-waveform-image
description: Generates a waveform PNG visualizing the amplitude envelope of an audio file.
example_prompt: Make a waveform picture of this mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's showwavespic filter renders the waveform to an image fully inside the WASM sandbox.
rationale: Podcasters and musicians need shareable waveform thumbnails and the audio never leaves the device.

name: base62-codec
description: Encodes bytes or numbers to Base62 (0-9A-Za-z) and decodes Base62 strings back, commonly used for short IDs and URL slugs.
example_prompt: encode 1000000 in base62
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — base-62 big-integer conversion is pure arithmetic.
rationale: Base62 powers short-link and compact-ID schemes, and developers regularly need to decode or generate these values.

name: base85-codec
description: Encodes and decodes Base85 in the Ascii85, Z85, and RFC 1924 variants.
example_prompt: decode this ascii85: <~87cURD]i,"Ebo7~>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Base85 is a deterministic radix-85 byte transform with no I/O.
rationale: Base85 is used in PDF, Git binary diffs, and ZeroMQ, and demand evidence shows people regularly need to round-trip it.

name: bech32-codec
description: Encodes a human-readable prefix and data to a checksummed Bech32/Bech32m string and decodes/validates Bech32 strings.
example_prompt: decode this bech32 address and check its checksum
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the BCH checksum, charset mapping, and HRP handling are deterministic local computation.
rationale: Bech32 is the SegWit/Lightning address format where checksum validation matters, and doing it locally keeps addresses off third-party servers.

name: binary-codec
description: Encodes text into a per-byte binary bit string and decodes a binary string back into text.
example_prompt: turn "hi" into binary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bit extraction and grouping are pure byte operations.
rationale: "Text to binary" is an extremely high-traffic conversion that is distinct from numeric base conversion.

name: bit-plane-view
description: Extracts and renders a single bit plane of a chosen color channel to reveal bit-level patterns and hidden data.
example_prompt: Show me bit plane 0 of the red channel of this image.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; bit-plane slicing is a local bitmask over the decoded pixels.
rationale: Bit-plane analysis is the go-to technique for spotting LSB steganography.

name: bitwise-calculator
description: Performs AND, OR, XOR, NOT, left/right shifts, left/right rotates, and bit population count on integers in binary, hex, or decimal.
example_prompt: What is 0xF0 AND 0x3C, then rotate the result left by 2 bits?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — native integer bit operations with base parsing/formatting, no external runtime needed.
rationale: Bit manipulation for masks, flags, and low-level/embedded work is constant developer demand and maps directly to AND/OR/NOT/shift/rotate terms.

name: blake2-hash
description: Computes BLAKE2b and BLAKE2s digests of text or a file with optional output length.
example_prompt: blake2b hash of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the blake2 RustCrypto crate is pure-Rust, deterministic and offline.
rationale: BLAKE2 is a fast, widely-adopted modern hash (used by argon2, libsodium, many CLIs) with real standalone demand.

name: bson-encode
description: Serializes JSON into BSON binary and returns it as base64 or hex for storage or transport.
example_prompt: encode this JSON as BSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the pure-Rust bson crate; binary output rendered as text, no server.
rationale: BSON interop with MongoDB and binary protocols is otherwise hard to do without a backend.

name: calculus-solver
description: Computes symbolic derivatives and definite/indefinite integrals with step-by-step output.
example_prompt: find the derivative of sin(x)*e^x and then integrate it
loader_feasibility: pyodide loader with SymPy performs symbolic calculus entirely client-side.
rationale: Covers a core WolframAlpha math workload that students and engineers search for repeatedly.

name: cartesian-product
description: Generates every combination (tuple) across two or more input lists, e.g. sizes × colors × materials.
example_prompt: Combine sizes S,M,L with colors red,blue,green into every possible pairing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — nested iteration over input lists producing text output, no external dependencies.
rationale: Building option matrices and test-case grids by hand is tedious and error-prone; this produces the full product instantly.

name: charset-decoder
description: Decodes byte input (hex or base64) interpreted under a specified character set back into readable text.
example_prompt: decode these bytes as Shift-JIS: 82a082a282a4
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via encoding_rs — decode tables run entirely client-side
rationale: Recovering mojibake'd text needs explicit charset control that copy-paste and ad-hoc tools rarely provide.

name: charset-encoder
description: Encodes text into a chosen character set (UTF-8/16, Latin-1, Windows-1252, Shift-JIS, etc.) and shows the resulting bytes as hex.
example_prompt: encode "café" as Windows-1252 and show the bytes
