name: random-list-picker
description: Shuffles a list or draws random winners/teams from supplied items.
example_prompt: pick 2 random winners from: Ana, Ben, Cara, Dan, Eve
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM shuffles via the browser CSPRNG in-process.
rationale: RANDOM.ORG demand includes fair draws/raffles done without trusting a server.

name: random-name-generator
description: Generates random realistic person or company names by region and gender.
example_prompt: Generate 10 random female German names.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sampling from embedded name lists with a user/host seed; no network.
rationale: A core Randommer capability that is trivially browser-local once the name lists are embedded.

name: random-number-generator
description: Produces true-random integers, decimals or sequences within a given range.
example_prompt: pick a random number between 1 and 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sourced from the browser CSPRNG; no network round-trip.
rationale: The core RANDOM.ORG use case, served instantly and privately.

name: remove-diacritics
description: Strips accents and diacritical marks from text while keeping the base Latin letters (café → cafe, naïve → naive).
example_prompt: remove the accents from: Mëtàl Ümläut Crüü
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: NFD-decompose then drop combining-mark codepoints, no model needed.
rationale: Directly requested as 'remove diacritics' and a common prerequisite for search keys, filenames and legacy-system input.

name: rison-to-json
description: Decodes a Rison string from a URL into readable JSON.
example_prompt: decode this Rison: (a:1,b:!t,c:!(x,y))
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure recursive-descent parse of the Rison grammar, fully offline
rationale: Reverse-engineering shared Kibana/OpenSearch dashboard URLs requires reading their Rison-encoded state.

name: rot47
description: Applies the ROT47 cipher across the printable ASCII range, covering letters, digits and punctuation (its own inverse).
example_prompt: ROT47 decode: %96 BF:4< 3C@H?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed-range codepoint rotation, deterministic and client-side.
rationale: A common alternative to ROT13 that also scrambles punctuation and digits.

name: rss-feed-discover
description: Scans pasted HTML for RSS/Atom feed links (link rel=alternate and common feed paths) and lists them.
example_prompt: find the rss feed url in this page source <paste HTML>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML link extraction, no fetch required.
rationale: Solves the discovery half of RSS Feed Search from copied page source.

name: shake-xof
description: Generates SHAKE128/SHAKE256 extendable-output (XOF) digests of a chosen output length.
example_prompt: shake256 of "seed" with 64 bytes output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the sha3 crate's SHAKE XOF reader is pure-Rust and produces arbitrary-length output offline.
rationale: SHAKE's variable-length output is a unique capability no fixed-digest tool offers, useful for key/nonce derivation.

name: sketch-to-icon
description: Recognizes a rough doodle and returns the matching clean icon.
example_prompt: Guess what this doodle is and give me a clean icon
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime running a small QuickDraw classifier model in-browser.
rationale: Reproduces AutoDraw's magic with an offline ML model.

name: sm2-sign
description: Produces an SM2 digital signature (r,s) over a message, computing the ZA user-identity hash with SM3 as the spec requires.
example_prompt: Sign this message with SM2 using my private key and user ID 1234567812345678
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2`/`sm3`; the per-signature nonce comes from the host secure-random import or RFC6979-style derivation, rest is pure compute in wasmi.
rationale: SM2 signing (not just encryption) is required for ShangMi-compliant auth and document signing, and the ZA pre-hashing trips people up enough to want a turnkey tool.

name: sql-minify
description: Collapses formatted SQL into a single compact line for embedding in code or logs.
example_prompt: minify this SQL statement
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM whitespace/comment-stripping tokenizer; fully local.
rationale: Compacting SQL for one-line embedding in source or config is a frequent chore.

name: strip-http-headers
description: Removes the header block from a raw HTTP message and returns just the body.
example_prompt: Strip the headers from this HTTP response and show only the body
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust split-on-CRLFCRLF logic in WASM; deterministic and local.
rationale: Isolating an HTTP body is a quick, frequently needed cleanup step.

name: strip-line-numbers
description: Removes leading line-number prefixes from each line.
example_prompt: strip the line numbers off this pasted code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a per-line regex/prefix strip runs entirely client-side with no dependencies.
rationale: Copying numbered code from docs/editors leaves prefixes that must be removed before reuse.

name: tech-stack-detector
description: Detects frameworks, libraries, analytics, and CMS generators from a pasted HTML source by matching script src, meta generator, and class-name fingerprints.
example_prompt: what tech stack is this site built with? <paste page source>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string/regex fingerprint matching over pasted HTML, fully client-side.
rationale: Delivers BuildWith's core value on any HTML the user can copy, with zero hosted index.

name: test-credit-card-generator
description: Generates Luhn-valid sandbox card numbers (Visa/Mastercard/Amex) for testing payment forms.
example_prompt: Give me a Luhn-valid test Visa number for my checkout form.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Luhn computation with a seed; deterministic and offline.
rationale: A common Randommer dev-testing need; pure math and clearly for sandbox use.

name: text-3way-merge
description: Performs a three-way merge of two edited versions of text against a common base.
example_prompt: Three-way merge: here's the base, my version, and theirs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diff3 algorithm; pure text computation, browser-local.
rationale: Resolving divergent edits without a full git setup is genuinely useful for non-engineers and quick fixes.

name: text-to-hex
description: Converts text or raw bytes into a hexadecimal string with selectable delimiter and case.
example_prompt: convert "Hello World" to hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure byte-to-hex formatting, no dependencies or network needed
rationale: Hex encoding is one of the most-searched everyday dev conversions and has zero server cost.

name: time-unit-converter
description: Converts a quantity between time units — seconds, minutes, hours, days, and weeks.
example_prompt: convert 36 hours to days
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — unit scaling is trivial arithmetic with no external dependency.
rationale: Collapses convert-days-to-hours and convert-hours-to-days (and more) into one tool that answers many related searches.

name: to-ci-regex
description: Converts a literal string into a case-insensitive regex pattern (e.g. cat → [Cc][Aa][Tt]).
example_prompt: turn 'error' into a case-insensitive regex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: building the character-class pattern is pure string assembly with no external regex engine needed.
rationale: Hand-writing case-insensitive patterns for engines without an /i flag is tedious and error-prone.

name: transliterate-to-ascii
description: Romanizes any-script text to a best-effort ASCII approximation, covering non-decomposable Latin (ø→o, ß→ss) plus Greek, Cyrillic and CJK.
example_prompt: transliterate to plain ascii: Москва Ωmega Tōkyō
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the any-ascii/unidecode mapping tables compiled in; pure lookup, fully offline.
rationale: Goes beyond diacritic removal to handle scripts that don't decompose, enabling ASCII-only identifiers and search across languages.

name: triangle-solver
description: Solves a triangle from any valid combination of sides and angles using the laws of sines and cosines, reporting all unknowns and area.
example_prompt: solve a triangle with sides a=5, b=7 and angle C=60 degrees
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM trigonometric computation, no network.
rationale: A specific high-value geometry workflow from MathIsFun/WolframAlpha that benefits from automation.

name: truncate-time
description: Truncates or rounds a date/time down to the nearest minute, hour, or day.
example_prompt: truncate 2026-06-19 14:37:52 to the nearest hour
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — flooring calendar fields is deterministic arithmetic with no network.
rationale: Satisfies the truncate-clock-time demand, frequently needed when bucketing events or normalizing timestamps.

name: unix-timestamp-to-date
description: Converts a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds or milliseconds) into a human-readable UTC/local date and ISO 8601 string.
example_prompt: what date is 1750000000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM integer/calendar math, fully offline.
rationale: One of the most frequent quick lookups for anyone working with logs or APIs.

name: vcard-generator
description: Creates a downloadable .vcf contact card from name, phone, and email fields.
example_prompt: Make a vCard for Jane Doe, jane@acme.com, +1 555 0100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits the vCard text format directly.
rationale: Lightweight Communication tool that's surprisingly fiddly to do by hand.

name: vigenere-keylength
description: Estimates the likely key length of a Vigenère cipher by computing the Index of Coincidence across candidate periods.
example_prompt: guess the vigenere key length for this ciphertext
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — slices text into columns and runs IoC per period, all in-memory
rationale: Key-length estimation is the hard step in breaking Vigenère ciphers and directly applies the IoC demand signal.

name: weighted-average
description: Computes a weighted mean from value/weight pairs, e.g. for grades or portfolio allocations.
example_prompt: My grades are 90 (weight 0.3), 80 (weight 0.5), 70 (weight 0.2) — what's my weighted average?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sum-of-products over weight divided by total weight, purely local.
rationale: Weighted averages are a common real-world variant of the mean demand (grades, GPAs, weighted scores) with no quick interactive tool.

name: whitespace-cleaner
description: Trims trailing whitespace, collapses blank lines, and normalizes the final newline.
example_prompt: Clean up trailing spaces and extra blank lines in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line normalization; pure string processing, no backend.
rationale: Whitespace noise pollutes diffs and pastes, and a one-click cleanup is a small but constant win.

name: xml-minify
description: Removes inter-element whitespace and comments from XML to compact it without changing structure.
example_prompt: minify this XML document
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with quick-xml streaming rewrite; no external dependencies.
rationale: Useful for trimming verbose XML/RSS/SVG markup before transport or embedding.

name: xxtea-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the XXTEA block cipher using a 128-bit key.
example_prompt: Decrypt this XXTEA ciphertext with key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure integer arithmetic XXTEA implementation, no deps or network.
rationale: XXTEA is widely embedded in games and IoT firmware; covers both encrypt and decrypt demand.

name: adler32-checksum
description: Computes the Adler-32 checksum of pasted text or an uploaded file.
example_prompt: What's the Adler-32 checksum of this data?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the adler crate; two rolling modular sums run locally.
rationale: Adler-32 is used in zlib and PNG, and devs need to verify it without uploading payloads.

name: amf-codec
description: Decodes and encodes Action Message Format (AMF0/AMF3) binary payloads to and from readable JSON.
example_prompt: decode this AMF0 payload (hex): 020005 68656c6c6f
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AMF is a self-contained binary serialization format parsed from bytes in-memory, no runtime needed.
rationale: AMF round-tripping is nearly impossible to find in-browser yet still appears in legacy Flash/RTMP and game traffic analysis.

name: arithmetic-sequence
description: Generates an arithmetic or geometric sequence from a start value, step/ratio, and count.
example_prompt: generate an arithmetic sequence starting at 3, step 7, 10 terms
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterative generation; deterministic local computation
rationale: Directly harvested demand term; useful for test data, schedules, and math practice.

name: barcode-generator
description: Generates Code128/EAN/UPC barcode label images from a number or string.
example_prompt: Generate a Code128 barcode for SKU AB-99421
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM `barcoders` crate renders to SVG/PNG in-page.
rationale: Inventory and shipping label workflows need barcodes and benefit from an offline, private generator.

name: bill-splitter
description: Splits a bill among people including tax, tip, and uneven shares.
example_prompt: Split a $84.50 bill with 18% tip among 3 people, I had the $30 dish
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic; trivial local computation.
rationale: A clean, instant bill/register calculation is a high-frequency everyday utility.

name: binary-to-text
description: Decodes space- or byte-delimited binary back into readable UTF-8 text.
example_prompt: decode 01001000 01101001 to text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses bit groups into bytes then UTF-8, fully offline.
rationale: The decode direction is just as common when solving CTF-style or teaching exercises.

name: boolean-expression-simplifier
description: Minimizes a boolean expression (AND/OR/NOT) into its simplest sum-of-products form via Quine–McCluskey.
example_prompt: Simplify the boolean expression A·B + A·B' + A'·B
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — implication-table minimization algorithm running purely on the input terms, no model or network.
rationale: Logic minimization is genuinely hard to do by hand and valuable for circuit design and exam prep, with few accessible local tools.

name: business-days-between
description: Counts working days (excluding weekends) between two dates.
example_prompt: business days between 2026-06-01 and 2026-06-30
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iteration over the date range, fully offline.
rationale: Distinct from a raw delta and a frequent need for SLAs, payroll, and project deadlines.

name: certificate-fingerprint
description: Computes the SHA-256, SHA-1, and MD5 fingerprints of an X.509 certificate (over the full DER) for trust comparison.
example_prompt: Give me the SHA-256 fingerprint of this certificate
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via PEM/DER decode + sha2/sha1; deterministic hashing performed entirely locally.
rationale: Fingerprint matching is the everyday way to pin or verify a certificate and is trivial yet frequently searched.

name: charcode-codec
description: Converts text to a list of Unicode/ASCII character codes (in a chosen base) and reconstructs text from a list of codes.
example_prompt: what are the character codes for "café"?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — code-point iteration and radix formatting run entirely in-memory.
rationale: Char-code lookups are a common need for debugging encoding issues and emoji/unicode work, with clear two-way demand.

name: citrix-ctx1-cipher
description: Encodes and decodes Citrix CTX1 obfuscated passwords as found in legacy ICA/connection files.
example_prompt: Decode this Citrix CTX1 password: NBA2EOLEEDGBEK
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the fixed XOR/transform scheme is pure byte math with no dependencies.
rationale: A specific, recurring admin/forensics need with steady search demand and almost no maintained tooling.

name: colormap-preview
description: Generates gradient swatches and legends for scientific colormaps (viridis, magma, plasma, turbo) with hex stops.
example_prompt: Show me the viridis and magma colormaps as gradient swatches
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates colormap functions and emits SVG/PNG swatches entirely client-side.
rationale: Choosing a perceptually-uniform colormap is a recurring need for anyone building heatmaps or data viz.

name: combinations-permutations
description: Computes nCr/nPr counts and optionally enumerates the actual combinations or permutations of a list.
example_prompt: How many ways can I pick 3 items from 10, and list all the combinations of [a,b,c,d]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — integer combinatorics and recursive enumeration, purely local computation.
rationale: Combinatorics counting and enumeration is high-demand for probability, lottery, and scheduling questions with no browser-local helper.

name: comment-stripper
description: Removes comments from source code across common languages.
example_prompt: Strip all the comments out of this JavaScript file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizer per language; local text transform, no server.
rationale: Stripping comments is useful for minification, sharing clean snippets, and counting real LOC.

name: convert-area
description: Converts an area value between units (m², km², ha, acre, ft², mi²).
example_prompt: convert 2 acres to square meters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; constant-factor area math runs client-side.
rationale: Area conversion is commonly needed for property, mapping, and engineering work.

name: convert-speed
description: Converts a speed value between units (m/s, km/h, mph, knots, ft/s).
example_prompt: convert 100 km/h to mph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure arithmetic conversion in-browser.
rationale: Speed conversion is routinely needed for travel, physics, and sports contexts.

name: coords-to-map
description: Plots one or more lat/long points onto a bundled offline world-map SVG with markers and labels.
example_prompt: show 48.8584, 2.2945 on a map
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; equirectangular projection draws onto an embedded world-map SVG — no tile server required.
rationale: Visualizing where coordinates fall is valuable and works offline without external map tiles.

name: crontab-generator
description: Build a valid cron expression from a chosen frequency, days and times.
example_prompt: make a cron expression for every weekday at 9:30am
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic field assembly, no external services.
rationale: Writing cron by hand is hard; generation removes the guesswork.

name: crypto-address-validator
description: Validates Bitcoin and Ethereum address checksums and formats.
example_prompt: Is this a valid Ethereum address?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM verifies base58/bech32 and EIP-55 checksums locally.
rationale: Catching a mistyped wallet address before sending is a high-stakes check that should never touch a server.

name: crypto-unit-converter
description: Converts between BTC/satoshi and ETH/gwei/wei units.
example_prompt: How many satoshis is 0.00125 BTC?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does fixed-ratio conversions with no live rate lookup.
rationale: Unit conversion is the browser-local slice of crypto demand (ShapeShift/Cryptrader) that needs no price feed.

name: css-border-radius-generator
description: Produces border-radius CSS including asymmetric blob shapes from up to eight radius values.
example_prompt: create an organic blob border-radius in css
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string output; pure computation.
rationale: Rounds out the CSS Matic toolset for shape styling without a GUI.

name: css-box-shadow-generator
description: Generates box-shadow CSS (including multi-layer and inset) from offset, blur, spread, and color inputs.
example_prompt: give me a soft elevated box-shadow css for a card
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template generation, no runtime dependencies.
rationale: Covers another high-traffic CSS Matic generator with natural-language inputs.

name: css-clamp-generator
description: Computes a fluid responsive CSS clamp() value from min/max sizes and min/max viewport widths.
example_prompt: fluid font size css clamp from 16px at 320px to 24px at 1200px
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM linear-interpolation math, emits CSS text.
rationale: Modern responsive-typography need adjacent to CSS Typeset, with tricky math users want automated.

name: de-bruijn-offset
description: Finds the byte offset of a 4- or 8-byte value within a De Bruijn pattern (the cyclic_find counterpart).
example_prompt: find the offset of 0x61616167 in a cyclic pattern
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regenerates the pattern and searches for the subsequence in-memory
rationale: Pairs with the generator to complete the standard overflow-offset workflow without any external tooling.

name: de-bruijn-sequence
description: Generates a cyclic De Bruijn (pwntools-style) pattern of a given length and subsequence size for buffer-overflow offset finding.
example_prompt: generate a 200-byte cyclic pattern
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — De Bruijn construction is a pure combinatorial algorithm
rationale: Cyclic patterns are the canonical way to locate crash offsets in exploit development and run instantly client-side.

name: disassemble-x86
description: Disassembles raw x86/x86-64 machine code (hex bytes) into annotated assembly mnemonics with addresses.
example_prompt: disassemble these x86-64 bytes: 4889e5c3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a pure-Rust decoder like iced-x86/yaxpeax-x86 compiles to wasmi, no native toolchain
rationale: An offline x86 disassembler serves reverse engineers and CTF players who can't paste shellcode into a remote service.

name: domain-name-generator
description: Brainstorms available-style domain name ideas from keywords using prefixes, suffixes, blends, and TLD suggestions.
example_prompt: suggest domain names for a vegan meal delivery startup
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM combinatorial generation over an embedded affix/TLD list, no WHOIS lookup.
rationale: Captures IWantMyName's ideation step (the WHOIS availability check is server-bound and excluded).

name: drop-nth-bytes
description: Removes every Nth byte of the input (with optional start offset), the complement of take-nth-bytes.
example_prompt: drop every 3rd byte from this data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure stride filtering, runs entirely in the browser.
rationale: Pairs with take-nth-bytes to manipulate interleaved or padded binary streams.

name: ecdsa-signature-convert
description: Converts an ECDSA signature between DER (ASN.1) and raw fixed-length r||s (IEEE P1363/JOSE) formats in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this DER ECDSA signature to raw r||s format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the ecdsa/der crates; a pure byte reformatting with no network.
rationale: DER↔raw signature mismatches are a notorious JWT/WebAuthn interop bug and a dedicated converter fixes them fast.

name: ecdsa-verify
description: Verifies an ECDSA signature (DER or raw r||s) over a message against an EC public key.
example_prompt: Verify this ES256 signature against this public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the ecdsa crate; a self-contained local verification.
rationale: Verifying ES256/ES384 signatures is a frequent JWT-debugging task with no convenient offline equivalent.

name: eta-calculator
description: Estimate completion time or ETA from progress, elapsed time or throughput rate.
example_prompt: if I'm 40% done after 2 hours, when will it finish
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: simple projection arithmetic, no network.
rationale: Handy progress projection for tasks, downloads and trips.

name: gost-streebog-hash
description: Computes the GOST R 34.11-2012 Streebog cryptographic hash (256-bit and 512-bit) of text or hex input.
example_prompt: Give me the Streebog-256 hash of 'hello world'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the RustCrypto `streebog` crate — pure hashing, no I/O, runs entirely in the browser runtime.
rationale: Streebog is the GOST digest used for signatures and integrity checks and has no convenient browser-local implementation.

name: hamming-distance
description: Counts the number of differing positions between two strings or the differing bits between two integers (XOR + popcount).
example_prompt: What is the Hamming distance between 1011101 and 1001001?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XOR and bit-count or per-character comparison, deterministic and local.
rationale: Hamming distance is widely used in error detection, coding theory, and bioinformatics and follows naturally from the XOR/bit-operation demand.

name: haversine-distance
description: Computes the great-circle distance and initial bearing between two latitude/longitude points in km or miles.
example_prompt: distance between 40.71,-74.01 and 51.51,-0.13
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — closed-form trigonometric formula, no dependencies
rationale: Geo-distance is a common calculation for mapping, logistics, and travel queries that runs instantly client-side.

name: heading-anchor-generator
description: Generates URL-safe anchor slugs (labels) for every heading in a document.
example_prompt: Give me GitHub-style anchor links for all the headings here
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM slugification rules; pure string transform, browser-local.
rationale: Consistent anchor labels matter for deep-linking docs and are fiddly to produce by hand.

name: hex-to-oid
description: Converts the DER hex encoding of an ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER into its dotted-decimal OID string.
example_prompt: What OID is the hex 06 03 55 04 03?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; trivial byte-level base-128 decoding with no dependencies or network.
rationale: A frequent ASN.1 debugging need that is tiny to implement and individually searched for.

name: hexdump
description: Renders a canonical hexdump (offset, hex bytes, ASCII gutter) from input and parses a pasted hexdump back into the original bytes.
example_prompt: make a hexdump of this string: GET / HTTP/1.1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — formatting columns and re-parsing offsets/hex/ASCII is pure string math.
rationale: Devs frequently need a `hexdump -C` view of payloads but have no client-side tool; round-tripping a dump back to bytes is uniquely useful.

name: hexdump-viewer
description: Renders input as a classic offset/hex/ASCII hexdump (xxd-style) with configurable column width.
example_prompt: show me a hexdump of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure formatting of bytes into aligned columns, no system calls
rationale: Developers reverse-engineering binaries reach for a hexdump constantly, and doing it locally keeps sensitive data off any server.

name: homoglyph-detector
description: Scans text for confusable/look-alike Unicode characters (e.g. Cyrillic 'а' posing as Latin 'a') and flags potential spoofing.
example_prompt: check this domain name for spoofed look-alike characters: paуpal.com
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the Unicode confusables table bundled in; comparison is pure lookup and runs offline.
rationale: Homograph spoofing is a real phishing/security concern and a defensive check users can run locally without sending text anywhere.

name: indent-converter
description: Converts indentation between tabs and spaces at a chosen width.
example_prompt: Convert this file from tabs to 2 spaces
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM indentation rewrite; local text transform.
rationale: Tab/space normalization is a recurring style-cleanup task that keeps diffs and linters happy.

name: integer-sequence-solver
description: Detects the rule behind an integer sequence (arithmetic, geometric, polynomial, linear recurrence) and predicts the next terms.
example_prompt: what comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fits differences/recurrences in-process, replacing an OEIS lookup for common patterns.
rationale: OEIS demand shows people constantly want to identify and extend number sequences offline.

name: ip-address-group
description: Groups a list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses into their containing subnets at a chosen CIDR prefix length.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — masking each address to the prefix and bucketing is integer math on parsed octets, fully local.
rationale: Collapsing scattered log IPs into networks is a core triage step for analysts and directly fulfills the harvested 'Group IP addresses' demand.

name: ip-to-ptr
description: Generates the reverse-DNS PTR name (in-addr.arpa / ip6.arpa) for an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
example_prompt: What's the reverse DNS PTR name for 8.8.4.4?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust string/nibble formatting in WASM; deterministic, no lookup needed.
rationale: Building the correct reverse-DNS name (especially the ip6.arpa nibble form) is fiddly and fully offline.

name: ipv6-address-converter
description: Expands, compresses, and normalizes an IPv6 address and shows its full and shorthand forms.
example_prompt: expand 2001:db8::1 to full form
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using std::net::Ipv6Addr parsing/formatting; pure transform.
rationale: IPv6 expand/compress trips people up constantly and is a natural companion to the ULA generator.

name: ipv6-expand-compress
description: Expands an IPv6 address to its full eight-group form or compresses it to canonical RFC 5952 shorthand.
example_prompt: Expand 2001:db8::1 to its full uncompressed form
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — zero-run detection and group padding are local string transforms over the parsed address.
rationale: IPv6 addresses appear in two visually different forms in logs and configs, and normalizing them is essential for matching and dedup.

name: ipv6-ula-generator
description: Generates a unique-local IPv6 (ULA) prefix per RFC 4193 from random entropy.
example_prompt: generate an ipv6 unique local address prefix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using getrandom (crypto.getRandomValues) for the 40-bit global ID plus SHA-1 hashing; all client-side.
rationale: Self-hosters need a properly-randomized ULA prefix, and generating it locally is both correct and private.

name: iso8601-duration-convert
description: Converts ISO-8601 durations (e.g. PT1H30M, P3DT4H) to and from seconds and a human-readable form.
example_prompt: how many seconds is PT2H15M
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string parsing and arithmetic, fully offline.
rationale: Common when working with APIs, video metadata, and schedulers that express durations in ISO-8601.

name: levenshtein-distance
description: Computes the Levenshtein edit distance (and optional similarity ratio) between two strings.
example_prompt: levenshtein distance between 'kitten' and 'sitting'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; dynamic-programming edit distance runs locally.
rationale: Edit distance underpins spell-check, dedup, and string-similarity scoring.

name: lm-hash
description: Computes the legacy LM (LAN Manager) hash of a password using its DES-based construction.
example_prompt: Generate the LM hash for 'WELCOME'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the des crate; the fixed-key DES construction is pure local computation.
rationale: LM hashes still surface in legacy Windows audits and need a quick offline generator.

name: mac-address-generator
description: Generates random or vendor-prefixed MAC addresses in selectable formats.
example_prompt: generate 3 random mac addresses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — uses host-provided crypto randomness and formats octets locally, no network.
rationale: Test fixtures, device emulation and lab setups frequently need valid throwaway MAC addresses.

name: mac-address-info
description: Parses a MAC address, reformats it across notations (colon/hyphen/dot/EUI-64), and flags unicast/multicast and globally/locally administered bits plus the 24-bit OUI prefix.
example_prompt: Tell me about the MAC 02:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust bit inspection in WASM; no vendor database bundled, so it stays small and local.
rationale: MAC reformatting and bit-flag analysis is a quick, common networking utility.

name: mac-address-lookup
description: Identifies the hardware vendor for a MAC address using the IEEE OUI prefix.
example_prompt: Which vendor owns the MAC 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a bundled, compressed OUI prefix table makes lookups fully offline.
rationale: Explicit demand term; bundling the OUI database avoids any external API call.

name: mime-header-decode
description: Decodes RFC 2047 MIME encoded-words (=?charset?B/Q?...?=) in email headers into readable Unicode text.
example_prompt: Decode this email subject: =?UTF-8?B?SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ=?=
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: base64/quoted-printable decode plus charset transcoding to UTF-8, all pure computation runnable client-side.
rationale: Garbled =?...?= subject and From lines are a constant pain when reading raw email, and decoding them locally keeps the contents private.

name: modular-arithmetic
description: Computes modular exponentiation (a^b mod m), modular inverse, GCD, extended GCD with Bézout coefficients, and LCM.
example_prompt: What is 7^256 mod 13, and find the modular inverse of 3 mod 11
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fast integer/u128 modular routines and the extended Euclidean algorithm, no external dependencies.
rationale: Modular exponentiation, modular inverse, and extended GCD are core to cryptography (RSA) and number-theory coursework and map the demand terms exactly.

name: morse-audio
description: Renders Morse code (from text) as a downloadable WAV file of beep tones at a chosen speed.
example_prompt: Make me an audio file of 'HELLO' in Morse code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — synthesizes PCM sine-wave tones and writes a WAV container in-memory; no ffmpeg or decoding required, fully client-side.
rationale: Turns Morse into shareable, playable audio entirely offline — a distinctive value-add no text tool offers.

name: murmurhash3
description: Computes the non-cryptographic MurmurHash3 (x86 32-bit and x64 128-bit) of input with an optional seed.
example_prompt: Give me the murmurhash3 128-bit of this string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the murmur3 crate; it is a few rounds of integer mixing, entirely client-side.
rationale: MurmurHash3 underpins many hash tables, bloom filters, and sharding schemes that developers need to reproduce.

name: oid-name-lookup
description: Maps a dotted OID to its friendly name (and vice versa) using an embedded dictionary of common X.509/PKCS/crypto OIDs.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a compiled-in OID table; a pure in-memory lookup with no network calls.
rationale: Turns opaque OIDs from certificate dumps into meaningful names, saving constant reference-table lookups.

name: parse-http2-frame
description: Decodes HTTP/2 binary frames (length, type, flags, stream id) and the payloads of structured frames like SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE, RST_STREAM, and PING.
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust frame parser in WASM; deterministic and local (HEADERS payloads are surfaced as raw HPACK).
rationale: HTTP/2 is binary and hard to read by hand, so an offline frame decoder fills a real gap.

name: parse-user-agent
description: Parses a User-Agent string into structured browser, engine, OS, and device fields.
example_prompt: Parse this user agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0 Safari/537.36
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with bundled UA pattern tables; pure string matching, no network or model, so it runs fully in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: User-agent parsing is a constant log-analysis and analytics chore that is fully deterministic offline.

name: power-set
description: Lists all subsets of a given set, optionally filtered by subset size.
example_prompt: Give me every possible subset of {a, b, c, d}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bitmask enumeration over set elements, runs locally with no model.
rationale: Enumerating subsets is common for combinatorics coursework, feature-flag combinations, and test coverage but has no easy interactive tool.

name: public-key-from-certificate
description: Extracts the subject public key from an X.509 certificate and outputs it as PEM (and optionally JWK).
example_prompt: Extract the public key from this certificate as PEM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via x509-parser + spki; a local extraction and re-encoding with no network.
rationale: Pulling the public key out of a cert is a frequent setup step for signature verification and JWKS publishing.

name: quoted-printable-codec
description: Encodes and decodes MIME Quoted-Printable, the =XX hex escaping used in email bodies and headers.
example_prompt: decode this quoted-printable: =C3=A9t=C3=A9
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — QP is a deterministic byte-escaping scheme with no I/O.
rationale: Anyone inspecting raw email or MIME parts needs to decode Quoted-Printable, and few clean browser tools exist.

name: quoted-printable-decode
description: Decodes quoted-printable text (=XX escapes and soft line breaks) back to its original UTF-8 bytes.
example_prompt: Decode this quoted-printable: Hello=20World=21
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: a simple byte-level state machine that runs fully local.
rationale: Quoted-printable is everywhere in email and form posts, and decoding it inline saves a trip to a sketchy web converter.

name: quoted-printable-encode
description: Encodes arbitrary text into quoted-printable with proper =XX escaping and 76-column soft line wraps.
example_prompt: Quoted-printable encode: naïve café — résumé
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: deterministic byte-by-byte escaping with no network.
rationale: Round-trips with the decoder so users can both produce and read MIME bodies when crafting or testing emails.

name: random-integer-generator
description: Generates one or many pseudo-random integers in a chosen range, with optional seed for reproducibility and no-duplicates mode.
example_prompt: give me 5 random numbers between 1 and 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a seedable PRNG (or browser crypto via host) runs without any server
rationale: Quick, reproducible random integers are a common everyday utility and need no remote randomness source.

name: randomize-case
description: Randomly alternates the case of each letter to produce mocking/sponge-case text.
example_prompt: Randomize the case of this sentence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded per-character case flip runs locally with no model.
rationale: Explicit demand term with popular meme/social use.

name: roman-numeral-converter
description: Convert between Roman numerals and integers in both directions.
example_prompt: convert 2026 to roman numerals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: simple mapping arithmetic.
rationale: A simple, frequently searched conversion that fits chat well.

name: rot13
description: Applies the ROT13 letter-substitution cipher to text (it is its own inverse).
example_prompt: ROT13 this: Uryyb jbeyq
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure character mapping, no network or native deps, runs fully client-side.
rationale: The most-requested classic cipher; instant, offline and private in the chat.

name: sfx-generator
description: Synthesizes retro 8-bit game sound effects (jump, laser, pickup, explosion) as WAV.
example_prompt: Generate a retro coin pickup sound effect
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DSP synthesizes waveforms and writes a WAV buffer, no assets needed.
rationale: Directly answers the 'bfxr' demand term for indie game-dev sound effects.

name: shuffle-lines
description: Randomly reorders the lines of text.
example_prompt: shuffle these lines into a random order
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a pure-Rust seeded PRNG (Fisher–Yates) shuffles the line vector entirely client-side with an optional user seed.
rationale: Randomizing a list (names, questions, picks) is a frequent need and works fully offline with a seed.

name: sm3-hash
description: Computes the SM3 (GM/T 0004) 256-bit cryptographic hash of arbitrary text or hex/base64 input.
example_prompt: Compute the SM3 hash of 'hello world'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm3`; streaming hash over CPU only, no I/O, runs in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: SM3 underpins SM2's KDF/ZA and is mandated alongside it in ShangMi stacks, so a standalone digest tool rounds out the suite and has independent demand.

name: ssh-hassh-fingerprint
description: Computes HASSH (client) and HASSHServer fingerprints from SSH KEXINIT algorithm lists for SSH client/server identification.
example_prompt: Generate the HASSH fingerprint for this SSH client: kex=curve25519-sha256,ecdh-sha2-nistp256 enc=aes128-ctr,aes256-ctr mac=hmac-sha2-256 comp=none
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HASSH is just an MD5 hash of the semicolon-joined kex/encryption/mac/compression algorithm strings; pure string + hash work, no network.
rationale: HASSH is a standard SSH fingerprinting method used in threat hunting and asset inventory, and analysts currently bounce to CyberChef to compute it.

name: sudoku-solver
description: Solves a Sudoku puzzle from a grid you provide.
example_prompt: Solve this sudoku: 53..7.... 6..195...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM backtracking solver runs instantly client-side.
rationale: Maps the Games demand with a deterministic, satisfying offline tool.

name: take-nth-bytes
description: Keeps every Nth byte of the input (with optional start offset), useful for de-interleaving data.
example_prompt: take every 2nd byte from this hex string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; deterministic stride extraction, no external calls.
rationale: De-interleaving byte streams is a recurring reverse-engineering and forensics task.

name: text-encoding-brute-force
description: Tries decoding bytes across many character sets and ranks the candidates by readability to identify the correct encoding.
example_prompt: brute force the encoding of these mystery bytes and tell me which charset is right
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via encoding_rs + chardetng — detection heuristics are pure Rust, no network
rationale: Fixing garbled text from unknown sources is painful without an automated charset guesser, and it runs instantly offline.

name: text-to-binary
description: Converts text to its binary (and optionally octal/decimal) representation and back.
example_prompt: convert "Hi" to binary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte-to-bit formatting is pure computation in the sandbox.
rationale: Encoding lessons, puzzles and low-level debugging routinely need quick text↔binary conversion.

name: timestamp-unit-detect
description: Given a raw numeric timestamp, detects whether it is in seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, nanoseconds, or Windows FILETIME and shows the decoded date for each interpretation.
example_prompt: what date is the timestamp 133592040000000000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM range heuristics plus conversion math, no external calls.
rationale: Saves users from guessing the unit of an unknown timestamp before they can convert it.

name: tlv-parser
description: Parses generic Type-Length-Value (BER-TLV / EMV-style) hex into a nested tag tree with decoded lengths.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive length-prefixed byte walker, fully client-side
rationale: Smartcard/EMV and protocol engineers debug TLV blobs constantly, and a local parser avoids leaking payment data.

name: todo-extractor
description: Extracts all TODO/FIXME/HACK annotations from code comments with line numbers.
example_prompt: Find every TODO and FIXME in this code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM comment scan; pure parsing, browser-local.
rationale: Surfacing scattered action items from a codebase is a quick way to build a cleanup backlog.

name: typing-practice-generator
description: Generates typing-practice passages at a chosen length and difficulty (common words, punctuation, numbers, code).
example_prompt: Give me a hard typing practice paragraph with punctuation and numbers.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM assembles text from embedded word lists with a user/host-supplied seed; no network.
rationale: TypingWeb's core value is practice material; generating it fits the tool model better than an interactive WPM widget.

name: ulid-generator
description: Generates ULIDs (lexicographically sortable, timestamp-prefixed unique identifiers).
example_prompt: generate 5 ulids
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — combines the host clock and crypto randomness with Crockford base32 encoding, all local.
rationale: ULIDs are an increasingly popular UUID alternative and developers want them generated without a server.

name: unicode-character-search
description: Searches Unicode characters by name or keyword and returns copyable glyphs with code points.
example_prompt: find me arrow symbols I can copy
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM searches a bundled Unicode name table; fully offline.
rationale: CopyPasteCharacter demand shows constant need for a special-character picker.

name: unicode-inspector
description: Breaks text into individual characters and reports each codepoint, official Unicode name, general category, block and UTF-8/UTF-16 byte encoding.
example_prompt: inspect every character in: naïve 𝕏 →
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using unicode-names2 / unicode-properties crates; the name tables bundle into the wasm and run offline.
rationale: Indispensable for debugging mysterious characters, encoding bugs and copy-paste artifacts, and complements the format generators.

name: unix-permissions
description: Parses Unix file permissions between octal, symbolic (rwxr-xr-x), and a plain-English explanation.
example_prompt: what does chmod 755 mean
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; bitmask parsing and formatting run in-browser.
rationale: Translating octal/symbolic permission modes is a constant source of confusion for developers.

name: varint-decode
description: Decodes base-128 varint bytes back into integers, supporting unsigned, two's-complement signed, and zigzag interpretations.
example_prompt: Decode the varint bytes ac02
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust accumulator loop in WASM; runs in-browser.
rationale: Decoding varints is a frequent step when manually reading protobuf or LEB128 streams.

name: varint-encode
description: Encodes integers as protobuf/LEB128 base-128 varints, with optional zigzag encoding for signed values.
example_prompt: Encode 300 as a protobuf varint
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust bit-shifting in WASM; deterministic and local.
rationale: Varint encoding underpins protobuf/WASM/DWARF and is a useful low-level primitive offline.

name: vigenere-cipher
description: Encodes or decodes text with the Vigenère keyword cipher.
example_prompt: Decode 'LXFOPVEFRNHR' with the Vigenère key LEMON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — keyword-driven shift arithmetic, deterministic and client-side.
rationale: Covers both Vigenère Encode and Decode demand in one tool; a classic-crypto mainstay.

name: vlsm-subnet-planner
description: Splits a parent network into variable-length subnets sized to each requested host count and reports the allocation map.
example_prompt: Subnet 10.0.0.0/16 into subnets needing 500, 200, 50, and 10 hosts
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust VLSM allocator in WASM; purely computational, no network.
rationale: VLSM planning is a classic, error-prone networking task that benefits from an instant offline solver.

name: whirlpool-hash
description: Computes the 512-bit Whirlpool digest of text or a file.
example_prompt: whirlpool hash of "data"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the whirlpool RustCrypto crate is pure-Rust and runs deterministically offline.
rationale: Whirlpool is an ISO-standard hash with steady niche demand and almost no privacy-respecting browser-local generators.

name: windows-filetime-to-unix
description: Converts a Windows FILETIME value (100-nanosecond intervals since 1601-01-01) to a Unix timestamp and a readable date.
example_prompt: convert FILETIME 133000000000000000 to a normal date
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM 64-bit integer math, fully offline.
rationale: A zero-substitute need in Windows log and forensic analysis that maps the demand term exactly.

name: yubikey-otp-parse
description: Splits a 44-character YubiKey OTP into its Modhex public ID and token, and optionally decrypts the token with a supplied AES-128 key to reveal the private ID, counters, timestamp, and CRC.
example_prompt: Parse this yubikey OTP ccccccibhbfflnjvjfbnjuvkhfthjvfvfclr with AES key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: Modhex decode plus a single AES-128-ECB block decrypt via the pure-Rust `aes` crate, all done locally so the secret key never leaves the browser.
rationale: Lets security engineers validate and inspect YubiKey OTPs offline without sending secret keys to a server.

name: analyse-uuid
description: Decodes a UUID to reveal its version, variant, and (for v1/v6/v7) embedded timestamp and node information.
example_prompt: what version is this uuid and when was it made: 018f...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure bit/field parsing of the 128-bit value
rationale: Inspecting a UUID's version and timestamp is a frequent debugging task and the natural companion to the generator.

name: bacon-cipher
description: Encodes or decodes the Baconian cipher, mapping letters to 5-symbol A/B patterns.
example_prompt: Decode this Baconian cipher: AABBA ABAAA AAABA
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed 24/26-letter mapping table, deterministic and client-side.
rationale: Covers Bacon Encode and Decode; a common steganography and puzzle cipher.

name: base92-codec
description: Encodes binary/text to and decodes from Base92, a high-density ASCII-safe encoding.
example_prompt: encode the word hello to base92
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a fixed-alphabet big-integer base conversion done in-memory.
rationale: Base92 is requested but rarely available outside CyberChef, so a browser-local version fills a real gap.

name: bcrypt-inspect
description: Parses a bcrypt hash into its version, cost factor, and salt without verifying any password.
example_prompt: What cost factor and version does this bcrypt hash use?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parsing the modular-crypt format is pure string decoding.
rationale: Auditing the cost factor of legacy bcrypt hashes is a real security-review need.

name: caesar-cipher-solver
description: Brute-forces all 25 Caesar/ROT shifts and auto-ranks the plaintext by chi-square fit to English letter frequencies.
example_prompt: decode this caesar cipher: Khoor Zruog
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 25 shifts scored by chi-square against a built-in frequency table
rationale: Combines the chi-square and frequency demand signals into a one-click classical-cipher breaker.

name: cipher-identifier
description: Analyzes an unknown ciphertext and ranks the most likely classical ciphers (Caesar, affine, Atbash, A1Z26, rail fence, substitution, etc.).
example_prompt: What kind of cipher is 'Gsrh rh z hvxivg' likely to be?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — frequency-analysis and character-set heuristics run entirely on-device.
rationale: Turns the cluster of classical-cipher demand into a high-value first step users reach for before decoding.

name: css-font-stack-generator
description: Builds a robust CSS font-family stack with web-safe fallbacks and system-font defaults from a primary font name.
example_prompt: give me a css font stack with Inter as the primary font
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lookup of fallback chains, emits CSS text offline.
rationale: Practical typography utility adjacent to Google Fonts that developers reach for constantly.

name: decimal-codec
description: Encodes text into space-separated decimal byte values and reconstructs text from a list of decimal byte values.
example_prompt: give me the decimal byte values for "OK"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte enumeration and decimal formatting are pure in-memory work.
rationale: Decimal byte encoding is a distinct, searched operation that complements the charcode and binary codecs.

name: dice-roller
description: Rolls dice with standard RPG notation (e.g. 3d6+2) and shows each die and the total.
example_prompt: roll 2d20+5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the notation and uses the browser CSPRNG locally.
rationale: Popular randomness use case from RANDOM.ORG demand, especially for tabletop players.

name: discord-timestamp
description: Generates Discord dynamic timestamp codes (<t:unix:F>) from a date/time.
example_prompt: Give me a Discord timestamp for next Friday 8pm in my timezone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts the date to a Unix timestamp and formats the code locally.
rationale: Discord timestamp generators are a popular standalone utility and are pure local computation.

name: emojify
description: Sprinkles relevant emoji into text by matching keywords to emoji.
example_prompt: emojify: 'we shipped the rocket and celebrated with pizza'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches words against a bundled emoji dictionary.
rationale: Emojify demand maps to a quick, playful text-decoration tool.

name: endianness-swapper
description: Swaps byte order of a hex string or integer between big- and little-endian at 16/32/64-bit word sizes.
example_prompt: swap the endianness of 0x12345678 as a 32-bit value
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure byte reversal and grouping, no dependencies
rationale: Reverse-engineering binary formats and network protocols constantly requires flipping endianness by hand otherwise.

name: enigma-machine
description: Simulates the Enigma machine with configurable rotors, ring settings, reflector, and plugboard to encrypt or decrypt messages.
example_prompt: Encrypt 'ATTACKATDAWN' on Enigma rotors I II III, reflector B, plugboard AB CD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rotor stepping and wiring tables are deterministic state machines, no host calls.
rationale: Iconic, high-interest cipher with strong educational and CTF demand and no easy browser-local equivalent.

name: float-hex-codec
description: Converts an IEEE 754 single- or double-precision float to its hexadecimal/binary bit representation and decodes those bits back to a float.
example_prompt: show the IEEE 754 hex bits for 3.14
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — uses native f32/f64 to_bits/from_bits, fully deterministic and local.
rationale: Float-to-bits inspection is a real low-level debugging need with no good browser-local tool, matching the To/From Float demand.

name: from-ci-regex
description: Collapses a case-insensitive character-class regex back to its plain-text literal.
example_prompt: convert [Cc][Aa][Tt] back to plain text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing the bracketed classes and emitting one letter each is pure local computation.
rationale: Reverses the case-insensitive regex form to make verbose patterns readable again.

name: gost-key-wrap
description: Wraps or unwraps a symmetric key under a key-encryption key using the GOST 28147-89 key-wrap scheme (RFC 4357).
example_prompt: Unwrap this GOST-wrapped key blob with my KEK
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM built on the Magma cipher plus its MAC (imitovstavka) — deterministic byte math, runs client-side.
rationale: Covers GOST Key Wrap and Unwrap; secure key transport is required wherever GOST ciphers are deployed.

name: http-status-lookup
description: Looks up an HTTP status code (or name) and returns its meaning, category, and typical usage.
example_prompt: what does http 418 mean
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM static code→description table; instant offline lookup.
rationale: Developers constantly look up status codes, and an embedded reference is faster than a web search.

name: ip-format-converter
description: Converts an IP address between dotted-decimal, integer, hex, binary, and expanded/compressed IPv6 forms.
example_prompt: convert 192.168.0.1 to its integer and hex forms
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure integer/bitwise arithmetic on the address, fully offline
rationale: Network engineers frequently need IPs in alternate notations for ACLs, configs, and obfuscated links.

name: ipv4-integer-converter
description: Converts IPv4 addresses to and from their 32-bit integer representation.
example_prompt: Convert 192.168.0.1 to an integer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — packing/unpacking octets is pure bit math.
rationale: Small but recurring Network-demand task for developers and DBAs.

name: ipv6-transition-address
description: Decodes IPv6 transition formats (IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, 6to4, Teredo, NAT64/64:ff9b) back to the embedded IPv4 address and parameters.
example_prompt: Decode the Teredo address 2001:0:4136:e378:8000:63bf:3fff:fdd2
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust bit-extraction logic in WASM; no network needed.
rationale: Transition-address decoding is niche, hard to do by hand, and otherwise unavailable offline.

name: iso-week-number
description: Returns the ISO-8601 week number, day-of-year, and calendar quarter for a given date.
example_prompt: what ISO week is 2026-06-19
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM calendar math, no I/O.
rationale: Useful for sprint planning, payroll, and reporting that index time by ISO week or quarter.

name: leap-year-check
description: Determines whether one or more given years are leap years and explains why.
example_prompt: is 2100 a leap year
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the Gregorian divisibility rule is a few comparisons, fully local.
rationale: Directly answers the check-leap-years demand; trivial to build and reliably correct.

name: legacy-md-hash
description: Computes the obsolete MD2 and MD4 digests for legacy interoperability and forensic analysis.
example_prompt: md4 hash of this NTLM input
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the md2 and md4 RustCrypto crates are pure-Rust and run offline.
rationale: MD4 underpins NTLM password hashes and MD2 still appears in old certificates, so security/forensics users need them despite being deprecated.

name: ls47-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts text with the LS47 pen-and-paper cipher over its 7x7 character grid.
example_prompt: Encrypt 'attack at dawn' with LS47 using the password 'rosebud'
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with a small hand-written LS47 implementation; it's pure character-grid arithmetic, ideal for the sandbox.
rationale: LS47 is a niche but beloved human-computable cipher with no good browser-local tool today.

name: mac-to-eui64
description: Derives the IPv6 EUI-64 interface identifier and link-local (fe80::) address from a 48-bit MAC address.
example_prompt: What is the IPv6 link-local address for MAC 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — EUI-64 is a fixed bit-flip-and-insert transform on the MAC bytes; deterministic local arithmetic.
rationale: Mapping a MAC to its auto-configured IPv6 identifier is a recurring need for network troubleshooting and a clean extension of the MAC-formatting demand.

name: number-base-convert
description: Converts a number between binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal, and any arbitrary radix from 2 to 36.
example_prompt: convert 255 to binary and hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — integer parsing and radix output are pure arithmetic, no external runtime.
rationale: A programmer's base calculator covers the To/From Decimal, Binary, and Octal demand in a single high-utility tool.

name: objectid-parser
description: Parses a MongoDB ObjectId into its embedded timestamp, machine, process, and counter components.
example_prompt: what timestamp is in this ObjectId 507f1f77bcf86cd799439011
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; hex decoding and field extraction are pure computation.
rationale: Extracting the creation time from an ObjectId is a frequent backend debugging task.

name: offset-checker
description: Compares two or more inputs character-by-character and highlights the offsets where they match or diverge.
example_prompt: check the offsets where these three hashes differ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; positional comparison is pure computation, no server.
rationale: Spotting where similar strings, hashes, or hex blobs start to differ speeds up debugging.

name: parse-client-hints
description: Parses User-Agent Client Hints headers (Sec-CH-UA, Sec-CH-UA-Platform, Sec-CH-UA-Mobile, etc.) into structured brand/version/platform data.
example_prompt: Parse these client hints: Sec-CH-UA: "Chromium";v="120", "Not?A_Brand";v="24"; Sec-CH-UA-Platform: "macOS"
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM header tokenizer; purely computational, runs in-browser.
rationale: Client Hints are replacing the UA string and few tools decode them, making this a fresh, useful complement.

name: parse-csr
description: Decodes a PKCS#10 Certificate Signing Request, showing the subject, public key, requested extensions, and signature validity.
example_prompt: Decode this CSR and show me the subject and SANs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via x509-parser CSR support; a local structural decode with no network.
rationale: Verifying a CSR's contents before submitting it to a CA is a standard step that lacks a friction-free offline tool.

name: parse-ssh-host-key
description: Parses an SSH public/host key (ssh-rsa, ecdsa, ed25519) and reports its type, bit length, and SHA-256/MD5 fingerprints.
example_prompt: What's the fingerprint of this ssh-ed25519 key?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the ssh-key crate; pure parsing and hashing done entirely client-side.
rationale: Confirming an SSH host-key fingerprint before trusting it is a common security check that deserves a quick local tool.

name: prime-factorizer
description: Finds the prime factorization of an integer and tests whether a number is prime.
example_prompt: Factorize 360 into primes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — trial division and Miller-Rabin run locally with no network.
rationale: Fits the Math demand category; useful for education and cryptography prep.

name: prng-generator
description: Generates reproducible pseudo-random numbers, bytes, or strings from a seed using selectable algorithms (LCG, xorshift, Mersenne Twister, ChaCha).
example_prompt: Generate 10 reproducible random integers 0-99 from seed 42 using a Mersenne Twister
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded PRNG state advances deterministically on-device with no entropy source needed.
rationale: Reproducible seeded randomness is handy for testing and simulations, and existing web generators aren't deterministic or private.

name: psu-wattage-calculator
description: Estimates required power-supply wattage and headroom from selected CPU, GPU, and component counts.
example_prompt: what psu wattage do I need for a Ryzen 7 and an RTX 4070?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM summation over an embedded component-TDP table, browser-local.
rationale: Captures ChooseMyPC's most actionable, data-light feature (live parts pricing stays server-bound and is excluded).

name: punycode-codec
description: Converts internationalized domain labels to and from Punycode (xn-- ASCII form).
example_prompt: convert münchen.de to punycode
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `idna`/punycode algorithm is pure integer/string math.
rationale: Punycode conversion is needed to debug IDN domains, phishing look-alikes, and certificate/email validation.

name: relative-time-humanize
description: Renders a timestamp or date as a relative phrase like '3 days ago' or 'in 5 hours' measured against now.
example_prompt: how long ago was 2026-06-01
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM delta plus formatting over the current epoch passed by the JS host; no network.
rationale: Ubiquitous UI and conversational string need that reuses the delta primitive with a friendly output.

name: repeat-text
description: Repeats a string a given number of times with an optional separator between copies.
example_prompt: repeat "ha" 20 times
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM loop building a string; trivial CPU, fully local
rationale: Quick way to generate filler, separators, or test data without scripting.

name: reverse-text
description: Reverses text by characters, words, or lines.
example_prompt: reverse the order of these lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reversing a sequence is a pure transform; Unicode-grapheme handling stays fully in-WASM.
rationale: Reversing characters/words/lines is a common quick text manipulation with consistent search demand.

name: search-link-generator
description: Builds a shareable 'let me search that for you' link that animates a query for the recipient.
example_prompt: Make an lmgtfy link for 'how to center a div'.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL encoding of the query; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Reproduces lmgtfy's exact function, which is just client-side URL construction.

name: sm2-encrypt
description: Encrypts a message with an SM2 public key, producing C1C3C2 ciphertext in hex or ASN.1 DER form.
example_prompt: Encrypt this message with SM2 using this public key: 04a1b2...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2` (+`sm3` KDF); needs one ephemeral random scalar from the host secure-random import or a user seed, otherwise pure in-sandbox compute.
rationale: Directly maps the harvested 'SM2 Encrypt' demand and serves the large base of developers integrating with Chinese government/banking APIs that mandate ShangMi.

name: sm2-verify
description: Verifies an SM2 signature against a public key and message, handling the SM3-based ZA identity hashing.
example_prompt: Verify this SM2 signature against this public key and message
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2`/`sm3`; deterministic verification with no randomness or network, runs client-side in wasmi.
rationale: The natural companion to sm2-sign, letting developers check ShangMi signatures without standing up a Chinese-crypto backend.

name: text-int-codec
description: Converts text to a list of integer character codes and back, with selectable base and delimiter.
example_prompt: convert ABC to decimal char codes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — maps between UTF-8/codepoints and integers entirely in-memory.
rationale: A common bridge for moving strings through systems that only accept numeric arrays, and for inspecting raw char values.

name: truth-table-generator
description: Builds the full truth table for a boolean expression using AND, OR, NOT, XOR, and implication.
example_prompt: Generate the truth table for (A AND B) OR (NOT C)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a small boolean expression parser/evaluator over all input rows, deterministic and local.
rationale: Truth tables are a staple of digital-logic and CS courses and a frequent search, with no convenient browser tool that takes an arbitrary expression.

name: unicode-escape-codec
description: Escapes characters to \uXXXX / \u{...} sequences and unescapes them back to Unicode text.
example_prompt: escape the unicode in 'café 你好' to \u sequences
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — codepoint-to-escape mapping is pure string processing.
rationale: Essential for embedding non-ASCII safely in source code, JSON, and config and for reading escaped strings back.

name: unicode-normalize
description: Normalizes text between Unicode NFC, NFD, NFKC, and NFKD forms.
example_prompt: normalize this text to NFC: café
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `unicode-normalization` crate ships its tables into the wasm binary, running offline.
rationale: Normalization fixes invisible duplicate-glyph and combining-mark bugs that break search, dedup, and string comparison.

name: venn-counts
description: Counts the size of each region (only-A, only-B, only-C, and all intersections) across two or three lists.
example_prompt: Across these three customer lists, how many are in all three, and how many only in list A?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — set membership tallying over hashed items, runs entirely locally.
rationale: Region counts for two- and three-way overlaps are exactly what people need for audience/segment analysis and Venn diagrams, beyond simple two-set boolean ops.

name: audio-denoise
description: Suppress background noise and hiss from speech recordings to produce a clean voice track.
example_prompt: clean up the background noise in this voice memo
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: nnnoiseless is a pure-Rust port of RNNoise that compiles to WASM and runs locally (RNNoise WASM is already proven in browsers).

name: auto-subtitle
description: Transcribe a video/audio's speech and output a timed SRT/VTT subtitle file.
example_prompt: generate subtitles for this video
loader_feasibility: transformers.js Whisper (ONNX/WebGPU) with word/segment timestamps → SRT.
rationale: One of the highest-demand media tasks; goes beyond text-only audio-transcribe by producing timed captions.

name: background-remove
description: Remove the background from an image, leaving a transparent cutout.

loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs RMBG-1.4 / U2Net segmentation in-browser; output PNG chains into image-resize/convert via ref.
rationale: Background removal is a hugely popular paid feature elsewhere that runs entirely client-side here.

name: document-qa

name: heic-to-jpg

name: object-remove

rationale: Hugely popular security check, privacy-preserving by design, and trivially browser-local with no API key.

name: run-javascript

rationale: A JS playground is as essential as the Python one already on the backlog.

name: run-python

name: sqlite-query

name: summarize

name: archive-extract

name: aspect-ratio-calc

name: audio-extract

loader_feasibility: transformers-js/onnx Whisper translate task in-browser; no server.

name: audio-waveform

name: auto-enhance

name: avif-convert

name: broken-link-check

name: child-growth-percentile

name: csv-join

name: curve-fit

rationale: Regression/trendlines are a constant need in analysis and science with no current tool.

name: data-chart

name: data-cluster

name: data-summary

name: date-calc

rationale: Date math is an extremely common everyday calculation that timestamp-convert (format conversion only) doesn't do.

name: debt-payoff

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM amortization loop + chart; offline.

name: dictionary-define
description: Look up a word's definitions, part of speech, and usage examples from an offline dictionary.

name: dns-lookup

name: document-scan

name: document-translate

name: docx-to-pdf

example_prompt: Convert this Word doc to a PDF

name: egfr-calc

name: passive-voice-detect

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: rule-based heuristics over tokens (Hemingway-style), no model needed; runs locally.

name: passport-photo

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime segmentation for clean background + Rust resize/crop to spec; browser-local and private.
rationale: Passport/ID photo makers are high-demand and benefit hugely from staying private/on-device.

name: password-strength
description: Estimate a password's strength, entropy, and crack time, with weakness feedback.
example_prompt: how strong is the password 'Spring2026!'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (zxcvbn-style estimator).
rationale: Checking strength (vs the existing generate/hash tools) is a top security utility.

name: pdf-ocr
description: OCR a scanned/image-only PDF to produce a searchable text or text-layered PDF.

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime + plain WASM — render pages with pdfium then run an in-browser OCR model per page, all local.

name: pdf-redact
description: Permanently redact a PDF by removing the underlying text/images beneath black boxes (true redaction).

name: pdf-table-extract
description: Detect tables in a PDF and export them as CSV/JSON, preserving rows and columns.
example_prompt: Pull the tables out of this PDF as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — pdfium text + position extraction with local table-structure heuristics, no server.

name: pdf-to-docx
description: Convert a PDF into an editable Word .docx, preserving text flow, headings, and basic layout.
example_prompt: Convert this PDF into an editable Word document
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM PDF text extraction + docx generation; offline.
rationale: One of the most-requested conversions, missing despite many other PDF tools.

name: pdf-to-images
description: Render each PDF page to a PNG image.
example_prompt: Convert this PDF's pages to PNG images
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM via pdfium-render's browser-WASM rendering; output PNGs are chainable into image-resize/crop via ref.

name: pdf-to-markdown
description: Convert a PDF into clean structured Markdown (headings, lists, tables) rather than raw text.
example_prompt: convert this PDF report to Markdown
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust PDF parser to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Structured PDF-to-Markdown is increasingly needed for docs/RAG; pdf-extract-text gives only raw text.

name: percentage-calc

example_prompt: What's the percentage increase from 80 to 120?
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — direct arithmetic, fully local.
rationale: Percentage questions are among the most common everyday math tasks and easy to get subtly wrong by hand.

name: photo-restore

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime face-restoration model (e.g. CodeFormer/GFPGAN class) in-browser.

name: plant-identify

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime plant/iNaturalist classifier in-browser; no server.
rationale: Top consumer vision use case; generic image-classify can't name species.

name: plate-calculator
description: Compute which barbell plates to load (per side) for a target weight.

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM greedy plate math, offline.

name: plot-function

name: portrait-blur

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime person/segmentation model + plain-Rust depth-aware blur.

name: pregnancy-due-date

name: projectile-motion

name: qr-batch

name: qr-generate

loader_feasibility: plain Rust (qrcode crate → image) compiled to WASM renders a PNG locally.
rationale: QR generation is broadly useful, fully offline, and outputs a chainable image.

name: question-answer
description: Answer a question by extracting the relevant span from a supplied context passage (extractive QA).

loader_feasibility: transformers-js (DistilBERT-SQuAD); small extractive model runs fully client-side.

name: receipt-parse
description: OCR a receipt photo and extract structured merchant, date, line items, tax, and total.
example_prompt: Extract the line items and total from this receipt photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR + plain-Rust structured parsing; offline.
rationale: Major expense-tracking use case far beyond generic OCR.

name: recipe-extract
description: Fetch a recipe page and extract clean structured recipe data (ingredients, steps, time, yield), stripping the blog filler.
example_prompt: Extract just the recipe from this cooking-blog URL
loader_feasibility: web-fetch + Rust JSON-LD/Recipe-schema + readability parse; browser-local.
rationale: Stripping the life-story preamble from recipe pages is a famous pain point and a purpose-built improvement over generic JSON-LD extraction.

name: regex-from-examples

loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local regex-induction/generalization algorithm runs entirely in-block.

name: regex-replace

rationale: Sankey is a popular flow visualization not covered by the existing chart tools.

description: Compute a weighted course grade or the final-exam score needed to hit a target grade.

name: graphql-format
description: Pretty-print, minify, and validate a GraphQL query/SDL with consistent formatting.
example_prompt: format this GraphQL query
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust GraphQL parser to WASM — pure compute.

name: graphql-introspect
description: Introspect a live GraphQL endpoint and output its SDL schema and type list.
example_prompt: Fetch the schema from this GraphQL API

name: graphql-to-types
description: Generate typed models (TypeScript/Rust/Go/Python) from a GraphQL SDL schema.
example_prompt: generate TypeScript types from this GraphQL schema
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust codegen to WASM — pure compute.

name: graphviz-render
description: Render a Graphviz DOT description into an SVG/PNG diagram of nodes and edges.
example_prompt: render this DOT graph: digraph { a -> b -> c; a -> c }
loader_feasibility: plain WASM (Graphviz/viz.js compiled to wasm); layout + render run fully in-browser.

name: gravatar-url
description: Generate a Gravatar (and Libravatar) image URL from an email by hashing it.
example_prompt: gravatar url for joris@suppers.ai at 200px
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM email normalization + md5/sha256.
rationale: A standard avatar-bootstrap snippet developers repeatedly hand-build.

name: groupby-aggregate
description: Group a CSV by one or more columns and aggregate (sum/mean/count/min/max/median) without writing SQL.
example_prompt: Group this sales CSV by region and sum the revenue
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM grouping; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A no-code group-by serves users who want aggregation without composing SQL in sql-query.

name: handwriting-ocr

name: har-analyze

example_prompt: analyze this HAR file and tell me what's slowing the page down

rationale: Turns a raw DevTools export into actionable performance insight with no upload.

name: har-to-curl
description: Convert a request from a HAR capture (or a single entry) into an equivalent curl command.
example_prompt: Turn the login request in this HAR into a curl command
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local JSON parsing of the HAR and string assembly, no network.

name: hash-identify
description: Identify the likely algorithm(s) for a given hash from its length and character set.
example_prompt: What kind of hash is 5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM pattern rules, offline.
rationale: A staple security/CTF utility for triaging unknown hashes.

name: hashtag-suggest
description: Suggest relevant, well-formed hashtags for a social post or topic, ranked by relevance.
example_prompt: suggest hashtags for a post about a sourdough baking class in Austin
loader_feasibility: transformers-js keyword/embedding model + formatting rules; local.
rationale: Hashtag generation is a top creator/marketer need and is distinct from raw keyword extraction.

name: headline-generate
description: Generate several catchy title/headline options for an article, blog post, or topic.
example_prompt: Give me 5 headline options for an article about browser-based AI tools
loader_feasibility: transformers-js small text-generation model in-browser; runs fully local with no API.
rationale: Title/headline generators are among the most-used standalone copywriting utilities.

name: heart-rate-zones
description: Compute target heart-rate training zones from age and resting HR (Karvonen / max-HR methods).
example_prompt: What are my heart-rate zones if I'm 35 with a resting HR of 60?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM formulas; browser-local.
rationale: HR-zone calculators are widely used by runners and cyclists for training.

name: hex-to-css-filter
description: Compute a CSS filter() chain that recolors a black element to a target hex color.
example_prompt: give me the CSS filter to turn a black icon into #1da1f2
