rationale: Recoloring monochrome SVG/icons via CSS filter is a famous, frequently-needed trick.

name: histogram-chart
description: Bin a list of numbers and render a histogram with auto or explicit bin counts.
example_prompt: Plot a histogram of these response times
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM binning + plotting; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A distribution histogram from raw numbers is a basic stats need distinct from image-histogram.

name: hmac
description: Compute an HMAC (SHA-256/384/512/MD5) of a message with a secret key.
example_prompt: compute the HMAC-SHA256 of this payload with key 's3cret'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HMAC; no network.
rationale: Webhook/API signature verification is common and not covered by plain hashing.

name: holidays-calc
description: List public holidays for a given country and year, including movable feasts like Easter.
example_prompt: What are the US public holidays in 2026?
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local holiday rules (including computus for Easter) and fixed-date tables, no API.
rationale: Planning and scheduling frequently need holiday dates, and the rules are fully computable offline.

name: htaccess-generate
description: Generate Apache .htaccess rules for redirects, caching, gzip, and access control.
example_prompt: htaccess to force https and redirect www to non-www
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM templating.
rationale: Classic high-search-volume webmaster tool with no entry yet.

name: html-entities
description: Encode text to HTML entities or decode entities (&, ©, named and numeric) back to characters.
example_prompt: decode these html entities: Tom & Jerry — "classic"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (htmlescape/entity table); pure lookup, fully local.
rationale: A staple text utility for cleaning scraped/templated HTML that the existing html-to-text/markdown tools don't cover.

name: html-to-jsx
description: Convert raw HTML into React JSX (class→className, self-closing tags, style objects).
example_prompt: Convert this HTML snippet to JSX for React
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust HTML parse + JSX serialization in-browser; no server.
rationale: Ubiquitous React workflow (transform.tools) distinct from html-to-markdown/html-to-text.

name: html-validate
description: Validate an HTML document/snippet and report syntax errors, unclosed tags, and nesting issues.
example_prompt: validate this HTML and list errors: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM HTML parser with error recovery.
rationale: W3C-style validation is a common web chore with no in-chat tool (yaml-lint/markdown-lint exist but not HTML).

name: htpasswd-generate
description: Generate or update an Apache/Nginx .htpasswd entry (bcrypt/APR1/SHA) for a user and password.
example_prompt: Make an htpasswd line for user admin with bcrypt
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local password hashing in the specific htpasswd format, no network.
rationale: A specific, frequently-needed devops format that password-hash doesn't emit.

name: http-headers
description: Fetch a URL and show its HTTP response status and headers (content-type, caching, security headers).

rationale: Inspecting headers (caching, CORS, security) is a common debugging task that web-fetch doesn't expose.

name: iban-validate
description: Validate an IBAN's checksum and extract the country, bank, and account parts (and format it).
example_prompt: is this IBAN valid: DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: IBAN validation is a routine fintech and form task.

name: ical-generate
description: Generate a downloadable .ics calendar event (title, time, location, recurrence, reminders) from details.
example_prompt: make a calendar invite for a team sync next Tuesday 3pm for 30 minutes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM building the iCalendar text format; pure string assembly, no server.
rationale: Producing an .ics file from plain details is a practical scheduling convenience with broad everyday appeal.

name: ics-parse
description: Parse an .ics calendar file into a structured list of events (title, times, location, recurrence).
example_prompt: what events are in this .ics file?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Reading calendar files is the inverse of ical-generate.

name: ideal-gas-law
description: Solve the ideal gas law (PV=nRT) for any missing variable with unit handling.
example_prompt: Find the pressure for 2 mol of gas at 300K in a 10L container
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic + unit conversion; browser-local.
rationale: A common chemistry/physics homework and lab calculator complementing molar-mass and balance-equation.

name: ideal-weight
description: Estimate ideal body-weight ranges (Devine/Robinson/BMI-range) from height and sex.
example_prompt: What's the ideal weight range for a 5'9" male?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM formulas; browser-local.
rationale: Ideal-weight calculators are a common health utility distinct from bmi-calc and tdee-calc.

name: identicon
description: Generate a deterministic GitHub-style identicon avatar image from a username, email, or hash.
example_prompt: generate an identicon avatar for 'joris@suppers.ai'
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: hash + symmetric grid rendering via the image crate, fully local.
rationale: Privacy-friendly default avatars are widely needed and trivially deterministic in-browser.

name: ieee754-convert
description: Show the IEEE-754 binary/hex representation of a float (and decode bits back to a number).
example_prompt: what are the IEEE-754 bits of 0.1 as a 32-bit float?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM bit manipulation.
rationale: A perennial low-level debugging tool with no equivalent among the existing base/binary tools.

name: image-aesthetic-score
description: Score a photo's aesthetic quality (composition/exposure appeal) to help rank or cull a set.
example_prompt: rate the aesthetic quality of these photos
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime with a small NIMA-style model in-browser.
rationale: Photo ranking/culling is a real workflow and a small ONNX model runs locally.

name: image-auto-orient
description: Auto-rotate a photo to its correct orientation using the EXIF orientation flag and bake it in.
example_prompt: fix the sideways rotation on this phone photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM EXIF read + re-encode; local.
rationale: Sideways phone uploads are a perennial annoyance; image-rotate only does manual rotation.

name: image-border
description: Add a solid or padded border/frame (and optional inner margin) around an image in a chosen color and width.
example_prompt: add a 20px white border around this image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM canvas expansion + fill; pure compute.
rationale: Quick framing/matting is a simple but frequently requested touch-up for photos and thumbnails.

name: image-channel-split
description: Split an image into separate R, G, B, and alpha channel images (and recombine).
example_prompt: Show me the red, green, and blue channels of this image
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM pixel extraction, offline.
rationale: A staple inspection/compositing tool for designers and developers.

name: image-chroma-key
description: Remove a solid-color (green/blue) background from a still image to a transparent PNG.
example_prompt: Key out the green background from this photo
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM color-distance masking, offline.
rationale: Fast color-based cutouts for still images complement the ML background-remove and the video-only chroma-key.

name: image-classify
description: Classify the dominant subject of an image into labels.
example_prompt: What kind of dog is this? <image url or ref>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs ViT/ResNet ImageNet classifiers in-browser via ONNX.
rationale: A lightweight building block for tagging and routing images, cheap to ship on top of the ML loader.

name: image-color-isolate
description: Keep a chosen color and desaturate everything else (color-splash / selective color).
example_prompt: Keep only the red in this photo and make the rest black and white
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM HSV masking per pixel; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: The selective-color/color-splash effect is a recognizable, frequently-requested edit.

name: image-color-replace
description: Replace one color (within a tolerance) with another throughout an image.
example_prompt: change the red logo background to transparent white
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-pixel color match/replace.
rationale: Quick recolor/cleanup task distinct from chroma-key (video) and background-remove.

name: image-deskew
description: Automatically detect a tilted scan or document photo's angle and straighten it.
example_prompt: straighten this crooked photo of a receipt
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: Hough-line angle detection + rotation on the pixel buffer, no network.
rationale: Common pre-OCR cleanup step that pairs well with the backlog's ocr tool.

name: image-diff
description: Compare two images pixel-by-pixel and produce a visual diff highlighting changed regions plus a percent-changed score.
example_prompt: show me what changed between these two screenshots
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (decode both + per-pixel delta, like pixelmatch); pure local compute.
rationale: Visual regression/diffing is a common QA and design-review task with no equivalent in the current image set.

name: image-drop-shadow
description: Add a realistic soft drop shadow behind a transparent-PNG cutout (product shots, stickers).
example_prompt: add a soft drop shadow under this cut-out product image
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust blur/composite (image crate) to WASM — local pixel work.
rationale: E-commerce and product imagery commonly need a shadow after background removal.

name: image-duotone
description: Map an image's shadows and highlights to two chosen colors for a duotone effect.
example_prompt: duotone this photo in navy and orange
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM luminance remap to a 2-color ramp.
rationale: Distinct stylization beyond the generic filter set; popular in branding/design.

name: image-embed
description: Produce a CLIP vector embedding for an image for similarity search, clustering, or dedup.
example_prompt: give me the embedding vector for this image
loader_feasibility: transformers-js / onnx CLIP image encoder runs in-browser; mirrors the existing text-embed tool.
rationale: An image-side counterpart to text-embed unlocks visual similarity and cross-modal matching locally.

name: image-emoji-mosaic
description: Rebuild an image as a mosaic made of emoji.
example_prompt: turn this photo into an emoji mosaic
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM: tile-average matching against an emoji color table, rendered on canvas.
rationale: A viral creative effect distinct from photomosaic (which uses tiles of the image itself).

name: image-filter
description: Apply visual filters to an image (blur, sharpen, grayscale, sepia, brightness/contrast).
example_prompt: Make this image black and white and increase the contrast
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute shaders process pixels on the GPU in-browser (same path as imagine), falling back to plain WASM.
rationale: Quick photo adjustments are a familiar, broadly useful feature and showcase the WebGPU loader already in use.

name: image-gradient
description: Generate a linear/radial/conic gradient image from color stops at a chosen size.
example_prompt: make a 1920x1080 blue-to-purple diagonal gradient
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pixel synthesis; emits PNG.
rationale: Quick background/wallpaper/asset generation for design and slides.

name: image-halftone
description: Render an image as a halftone dot pattern (CMYK or single-color) for print and retro looks.
example_prompt: Give this image a comic-book halftone dot effect
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute — per-cell dot-size computation from local luminance, GPU rasterized, no network.
rationale: Distinct from dithering and popular for posters/comics; a known gap in the image toolset.

name: image-histogram
description: Compute and render an RGB/luminance histogram for an image to inspect exposure and tone.
example_prompt: show the histogram of this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (image crate) for analysis + plotting.
rationale: Standard photo-editing diagnostic that complements the existing image filters.

name: image-low-poly
description: Convert a photo into low-poly triangulated geometric art.
example_prompt: Turn this portrait into low-poly art
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM (Delaunay triangulation + average fill) or webgpu-compute; pure compute, local.
rationale: Trianglify-style low-poly art is a popular aesthetic for wallpapers and avatars.

name: image-meme
description: Add classic top/bottom impact-font caption text (with outline) to an image to make a meme.
example_prompt: make a meme from this image, top text 'WHEN THE TESTS', bottom text 'FINALLY PASS'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (decode + ab_glyph text with stroke); pure raster compositing.
rationale: A recognizable standalone product distinct from the generic watermark tool, with broad casual appeal.

name: image-motion-blur
description: Apply directional, radial, or zoom motion blur to an image.
example_prompt: Add a horizontal motion blur to this car photo
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute or plain Rust directional convolution; browser-local.
rationale: Directional/zoom blur is a distinct creative effect from the generic gaussian blur in image-filter.

name: image-oil-painting
description: Apply a classic oil-painting stylization filter (non-ML brush-stroke effect).
example_prompt: Make this look like an oil painting
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute or plain Rust convolution (Kuwahara-style); browser-local, no model.
rationale: A lightweight artistic effect distinct from neural style-transfer, fast enough to run on-device.

name: image-paint-by-numbers
description: Convert a photo into a paint-by-numbers template with outlined regions, numbers, and a color legend.
example_prompt: make a paint-by-numbers template from this photo with 16 colors
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM color quantization + region labeling.
rationale: A popular craft/print tool distinct from posterize and edge-detect.

name: image-palette
description: Extract the dominant color palette from an image.
example_prompt: Get the main colors from this image: <image url or ref>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust (image + color-quant/k-means) compiled to WASM computes the palette locally.
rationale: Palette extraction is popular for design work and is cheap on the existing image stack.

name: image-palette-remap
description: Remap an image's colors to a target palette (Nord, Solarized, Game Boy, custom).
example_prompt: Recolor this screenshot to the Nord palette
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM nearest-color quantization to a palette, offline.
rationale: Theming images/pixel art to a palette is popular and broader than single-color replace or duotone.

name: image-perspective-warp

example_prompt: Warp this photo's corners to straighten the building
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM homography sampling, offline.
rationale: General perspective warping is broader than the document-only scan/deskew tools.

name: image-posterize
description: Reduce an image to a few flat color bands for a poster / screen-print look.
example_prompt: Posterize this photo to 6 color levels
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM per-pixel quantization (or webgpu-compute shader); fully browser-local.
rationale: Classic creative filter not covered by the existing dither/pixel-art tools.

name: image-search
description: Rank a set of images by visual similarity to a query image using CLIP embeddings.
example_prompt: which of these images looks most like this one?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js CLIP image embeddings + cosine similarity, all in-browser.
rationale: Visual similarity search is distinct from image-dedupe (phash near-dups) and the raw image-embed tool.

name: image-segment
description: Segment an image into labeled regions/masks (e.g. person, sky, road) with a semantic model.
example_prompt: Show me a segmentation mask of this scene
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime or transformers-js segmentation model (e.g. SegFormer) runs in-browser; segmentation is a supported transformers.js task.
rationale: Pixel-level scene understanding underpins masking/editing workflows and extends the existing vision-model lineup.

name: image-steganography
description: Hide a secret message inside an image (LSB) and extract hidden messages back out.
example_prompt: hide 'meet at 8' inside this picture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM least-significant-bit encode/decode.
rationale: Fun + privacy use case that's a classic CyberChef-style tool absent here.

name: image-text-search
description: Rank a set of images by how well they match a natural-language query using CLIP.
example_prompt: from these photos, find the ones with a red car at night
loader_feasibility: transformers-js CLIP text+image embeddings in-browser.
rationale: Text-to-image search is core to modern photo libraries; existing image-search ranks by a query image, not text.

name: image-threshold

example_prompt: convert this scanned page to clean black and white
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (image crate) to WASM — pure pixel compute.
rationale: Document/scan prep and stencil/laser workflows need clean binarization.

name: image-tilt-shift

loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute or plain Rust graduated blur; browser-local.

name: image-to-datauri

example_prompt: turn this icon into a data URI I can inline in my CSS

rationale: Frequent front-end task for inlining small assets and avoiding extra requests.

name: image-vignette

example_prompt: Add a subtle dark vignette to this photo

rationale: A staple photo-finishing effect not covered by the existing blur/sepia image-filter tool.

name: image-watermark-remove
description: Auto-detect a repeating watermark or logo overlay and inpaint it away.
example_prompt: remove the stock-photo watermark from this image
loader_feasibility: onnx inpainting model (e.g. LaMa) in-browser.

name: images-to-animated-webp

example_prompt: make an animated webp from these 12 frames at 10fps

name: inclusive-language-check

example_prompt: Scan this job posting for non-inclusive language and suggest fixes
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: dictionary/rule matching (alex.js-style word list); pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Widely used in docs/HR/marketing review pipelines and not covered by grammar or redaction tools.

name: inflation-calc

name: ini-convert
description: Convert between INI/config and JSON in either direction.
example_prompt: convert this INI file to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM INI parser/serializer.

name: initials-avatar

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM canvas/raster draw; browser-local.

name: interpolate

name: ip-info

name: isbn-lookup

name: json-path-finder

example_prompt: Find the JSON path to the value 'expired' in this API response

name: json-schema-generate

name: json-sort

example_prompt: Sort all the keys in this JSON config alphabetically

name: json-to-zod

loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM type inference, same engine family as json-to-types.

name: json5-convert

name: jsonl-convert

example_prompt: convert this JSON array into JSONL for my fine-tuning dataset
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: streaming line parse, no server.
rationale: JSONL is the standard LLM dataset format, making this a natural fit for gizza's AI users.

name: jsonschema-mock
description: Generate realistic fake data that conforms to a given JSON Schema (respecting types, formats, enums).

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.

name: jsonschema-to-types

example_prompt: Remove stopwords from this paragraph for a keyword index
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — bundled per-language stopword lists applied with local tokenization, no network.
rationale: A common cleaning step for search/embedding pipelines that pairs with the existing keyword and chunk tools.

name: string-escape
description: Escape or unescape a string for JSON, JavaScript, SQL, shell, regex, or CSV contexts.
example_prompt: escape this multiline text so I can paste it into a JSON string
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: per-context escaping rules, no network.
rationale: Frequent embedding chore broader than the existing url-encode/html-entities tools.

name: style-transfer
description: Repaint a photo in an artistic style (e.g. Van Gogh, ukiyo-e, sketch) using fast neural style transfer.
example_prompt: make this photo look like a Van Gogh painting
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime fast-neural-style models (or webgpu-compute shaders); inference is fully local.
rationale: Artistic restyling is a popular creative effect with small pretrained models suited to in-browser inference.

name: subnet-calc
description: Compute network details from a CIDR/IP (network/broadcast address, mask, host range, count).
example_prompt: What's the host range and broadcast for 192.168.1.0/26?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM ipnet arithmetic; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Subnetting math is a staple of every IT/network toolbox (e.g. IT-Tools) and is purely computational.

name: subtitle-convert
description: Convert subtitles between SRT, VTT, and ASS formats.
example_prompt: convert this SRT to WebVTT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM format parser/serializer.
rationale: Format mismatches between players/platforms are common; distinct from extract/burn.

name: subtitle-shift
description: Shift all timestamps in an SRT/VTT subtitle file by a positive or negative offset.
example_prompt: shift these subtitles 2.5 seconds later
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM timestamp parse + rewrite.
rationale: Resyncing out-of-sync subs is a frequent, fiddly manual job.

name: subtitle-to-text
description: Strip timestamps and cue numbers from an SRT/VTT/ASS file to produce a clean, readable transcript paragraph.
example_prompt: turn this .srt into plain readable text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parser; local.
rationale: People constantly want the words from captions without the timing scaffolding; existing subtitle tools only convert/shift/translate.

name: sudoku-generate
description: Generate a fresh Sudoku puzzle at a chosen difficulty, with the solution.
example_prompt: Generate a hard Sudoku puzzle
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM generator + image render; offline.
rationale: Pairs with sudoku-solve and gives a printable puzzle.

name: sudoku-solve
description: Solve a Sudoku puzzle from a given grid and report whether it's uniquely solvable.
example_prompt: Solve this Sudoku (paste the grid)
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM constraint solver; offline.
rationale: Classic puzzle helper with steady demand.

name: sunburst-chart
description: Render a hierarchical sunburst (radial treemap) from nested or grouped data.
example_prompt: Make a sunburst of my disk usage by folder
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust radial layout + raster render in-browser.
rationale: The radial sibling of treemap for hierarchies, currently unavailable.

name: svg-blob-generate
description: Generate a random organic blob shape as an SVG (and PNG) with adjustable complexity and color.
example_prompt: Generate a purple organic blob SVG for my hero section
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust bezier path generation → SVG/PNG in-browser.
rationale: Heavily used web-design asset generator (10015.io, getwaves) missing from the toolset.

name: swim-pace
description: Compute swim pace, critical swim speed, and interval splits per 100m/100yd.
example_prompt: My 400m took 6:40 — what's my pace per 100m?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: Swimmers track pace differently from runners; the running-pace tool doesn't fit.

name: syllable-count
description: Count syllables per word and total, and hyphenate words at valid break points.
example_prompt: How many syllables are in "unbelievable"? And hyphenate it.
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — Liang hyphenation patterns + a pronunciation dictionary do syllabification locally.
rationale: Needed for poetry, lyrics, typesetting, and readability work that the existing readability tool doesn't cover.

name: systemd-unit-generate
description: Generate a systemd service unit file from command, user, restart, and dependency options.
example_prompt: Make a systemd service that runs /opt/app on boot and restarts on failure
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM templating, offline.
rationale: Self-hosters write these constantly; fits the existing nginx/dockerfile/htaccess generators.

name: table-format
description: Render tabular data (CSV/JSON) as a clean Markdown or ASCII table.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into a Markdown table
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM formatting; instant and offline.
rationale: Pasting data into docs/READMEs/issues as aligned tables is a frequent, low-effort win.

name: table-to-image
description: Render a CSV/JSON table as a clean, styled image (with header styling and zebra rows) for sharing.
example_prompt: render this CSV as a nice table image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM table layout + raster render; local.
rationale: Sharing data as an image is common; existing tools render Markdown or code, not data tables directly.

name: table-to-latex
description: Convert a CSV or pasted table into a LaTeX tabular/booktabs environment.
example_prompt: turn this CSV into a LaTeX table with booktabs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formatting; local.
rationale: Academics and report writers constantly need LaTeX tables; table-format only emits Markdown/ASCII.

name: tailwind-palette-generate
description: Generate a Tailwind-style 50–950 shade scale from a base color, as config/CSS variables.
example_prompt: Make a Tailwind color scale from #4f46e5
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust color-space math → swatches + config text in-browser.
rationale: Specific, popular front-end need distinct from generic palette/shade generators.

name: tailwind-to-css
description: Expand a string of Tailwind utility classes into the equivalent raw CSS.
example_prompt: What CSS does 'flex items-center gap-4 rounded-lg' compile to?
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust mapping of Tailwind tokens → CSS declarations; no network.
rationale: The inverse of the existing css-to-tailwind tool and frequently needed when reading Tailwind code.

name: taylor-series
description: Compute the Taylor/Maclaurin series expansion of a function to N terms and plot the approximation against the original.
example_prompt: give the Taylor series of sin(x) around 0 to 7 terms
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM symbolic differentiation + plot; local.
rationale: Series expansion is a core calculus tool that the existing differentiate/integrate solver doesn't produce.

name: tdee-calc
description: Estimate BMR, TDEE (daily calories), and macro targets from age, sex, weight, height, and activity.
example_prompt: how many calories should I eat to maintain at 75kg, 180cm, age 30, active?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Calorie/macro calculators are extremely popular health utilities; the BMI tool exists but not TDEE.

name: technical-indicators
description: Compute trading indicators (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, moving averages) from a price series and overlay them on a chart.
example_prompt: compute RSI and MACD for this daily close-price data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM math + SVG plot; local.
rationale: Retail traders heavily use these indicators; candlestick-chart only draws price + simple MAs.

name: text-autolink
description: Detect bare URLs, emails, and @mentions in plain text and turn them into Markdown or HTML links.
example_prompt: Auto-link all the URLs in these notes as Markdown
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM regex/parse; offline.
rationale: Tiny but frequently needed when pasting plain text into docs/CMS.

name: text-generate
description: Continue or generate text from a prompt using a small local language model.
example_prompt: continue this story: 'The lighthouse keeper noticed…'
loader_feasibility: transformers.js small causal LM (e.g. distilgpt2/SmolLM, WebGPU); no server.
rationale: Adds genuine generation (vs the transform-only paraphrase/summarize) fully offline.

name: text-normalize
description: Clean text by collapsing whitespace, converting smart quotes/dashes to ASCII, stripping zero-width and control characters, and fixing mojibake.
example_prompt: clean up the weird quotes and invisible characters in this pasted text
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: deterministic Unicode normalization, no network.
rationale: Solves a constant copy-paste pain point before publishing or feeding text to code.

name: text-shadow-css
description: Generate CSS text-shadow code, including layered, 3D, and neon glow presets, with preview.
example_prompt: generate a neon glow text-shadow in cyan
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM string assembly plus an inline preview.
rationale: text-shadow is distinct from the existing box-shadow-css and a common design ask.

name: text-steganography
description: Hide a secret message inside ordinary text using zero-width characters, and extract it back.
example_prompt: hide 'meet at 9' inside the text 'see you soon'
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM zero-width insertion/extraction.
rationale: Text-based counterpart to the existing image-steganography, with real watermarking uses.

name: text-to-handwriting
description: Render typed text as a realistic handwritten-looking page image with selectable pen styles.
example_prompt: Turn these notes into handwriting on lined paper
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — handwriting-style fonts plus jitter/baseline variation rasterized to a canvas locally.
rationale: A popular student/novelty tool with consistent demand and a fully offline rendering path.

name: text-to-regex
description: Generate a regular expression from a plain-English description of the pattern to match.
example_prompt: give me a regex that matches US phone numbers with optional country code
loader_feasibility: transformers-js small code model runs in-browser; best-effort output the user can verify with regex-test.
rationale: Writing regex from a description is one of the most-searched dev tasks; complements the existing example-based and explain tools.

name: text-to-svg
description: Convert text in a chosen font into editable SVG outline paths (for logos, laser cutters, Cricut).
example_prompt: convert the word 'MAKER' to SVG paths in a bold font
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM font shaping to vector paths; local.
rationale: Makers and designers need text-as-paths for cutting/engraving; vectorize only traces raster images.

name: time-card
description: Compute a timesheet: sum daily clock-in/out spans minus breaks into total hours and pay.
example_prompt: total my week: Mon 9-5 (30m lunch), Tue 9-6 (1h lunch)... at $25/hr
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM time math.
rationale: A common worker tool distinct from the simple time-duration-add.

name: time-duration-add
description: Add, subtract, and total durations (HH:MM:SS) — e.g. summing clip lengths or work hours.
example_prompt: Add up these video durations: 12:30, 4:05, and 1:22:10
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM time arithmetic; browser-local.
rationale: Summing time-of-day durations is a common chore distinct from date-calc's calendar math.

name: time-series-resample
description: Resample/aggregate a timestamped series to a coarser interval (e.g. minute→hour, day→week).
example_prompt: resample this daily CSV to weekly sums
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM time bucketing.
rationale: A fundamental time-series operation distinct from categorical groupby-aggregate and data-smooth.

name: timeline-chart
description: Render a horizontal timeline of dated events with labels.
example_prompt: timeline of these milestones: 2020 founded, 2022 seed, 2024 series A
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM SVG/PNG render.
rationale: Event timelines are a distinct, common viz from the task-and-dependency gantt-chart.

name: tip-split
description: Calculate tip and split a bill across people, with per-person totals and optional rounding.
example_prompt: Split a $134.50 bill with 18% tip among 4 people
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — direct arithmetic, fully local.
rationale: An extremely common real-world calculation people do on their phones constantly.

name: tire-size-compare
description: Compare two tire sizes for diameter, circumference, and speedometer error.
example_prompt: Compare 225/45R17 vs 235/40R18 — what's the speedo error?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM geometry, offline.
rationale: A very common automotive lookup when changing wheels/tires.

name: toml-convert
description: Convert between TOML and JSON in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this Cargo.toml section to JSON
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM with the toml + serde_json crates; offline, mirrors the yaml-to-json/xml-to-json backlog.
rationale: TOML is everywhere in Rust/Python tooling and rounds out the config-format conversion set already on the backlog.

name: tone-generate
description: Synthesize a test tone (sine/square/sweep) at a given frequency and duration.
example_prompt: generate a 440Hz sine tone for 3 seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM PCM synthesis (or ffmpeg aevalsrc).
rationale: Useful for speaker/hearing tests, tuning references, and audio calibration.

name: tournament-bracket
description: Render a single- or double-elimination bracket image from a list of competitors.
example_prompt: make a single-elim bracket for 8 teams: <list>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM SVG/PNG render.
rationale: Popular for sports/games; different from random-team-picker which only splits groups.

name: toxicity-detect
description: Score text for toxicity, insults, threats, and hate so it can be flagged or moderated before posting.
example_prompt: is this comment toxic? <paste comment>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js (toxic-bert / unbiased-toxic-roberta); classification model runs in-browser.
rationale: Content-moderation scoring is a common need for forums and UGC that the existing sentiment/redact tools don't address.

name: train-test-split
description: Split a CSV into train/test (and optional validation) sets with stratification and a reproducible seed.
example_prompt: Split this dataset 80/20 into train and test, stratified by label
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM seeded shuffle + partition; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A reproducible train/test split is a routine first step in any ML workflow.

name: transcript-clean
description: Clean a raw transcript: remove filler words, fix capitalization/punctuation, and merge speaker turns.
example_prompt: Clean up this messy auto-transcript and remove the ums
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust rules + optional transformers-js punctuation model; browser-local.
rationale: Polishing raw transcripts into readable text is a common step after transcription.

name: treemap-chart
description: Render a hierarchical treemap sized by value from nested or grouped data.
example_prompt: treemap this CSV of disk usage by folder
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust rendering to PNG/SVG, client-side.
rationale: Treemaps are a common way to show part-of-whole hierarchies.

name: truth-table
description: Generate a full truth table for a boolean expression with AND/OR/NOT/XOR/implication and report tautology/contradiction.
example_prompt: make a truth table for (A AND B) OR NOT C
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: parse + enumerate all input rows locally.
rationale: Staple for CS/logic students with no equivalent in the existing math tools.

name: ts-decompose
description: Decompose a time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components and plot them.
example_prompt: decompose this monthly sales series into trend and seasonality
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM STL/classical decomposition + SVG plot; local.
rationale: Seeing trend vs seasonality is fundamental to forecasting and isn't provided by the forecast or smoothing tools.

name: type-scale
description: Generate a modular typographic scale (font sizes and line heights) from a base size and ratio, as CSS or tokens.
example_prompt: make a 1.25 modular type scale from 16px base
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Type scales are a standard design-system building block.

name: typographic-fix
description: Apply smart typography: straight quotes to curly, -- to en/em dashes, ... to an ellipsis (a 'smartypants' pass).
example_prompt: Fix the typography in this paragraph for publishing
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM string transform; offline.
rationale: Inverse of the existing text-normalize tool and a real publishing/writing need.

name: ulid-inspect
description: Decode a ULID into its embedded timestamp and randomness (and validate it).
example_prompt: What time is encoded in this ULID?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM base32 decode, offline.
rationale: ULID decoding is missing even though UUID/ObjectId/Snowflake inspectors exist.

name: unicode-confusables-detect
description: Detect homoglyph/confusable characters and invisible code points used in phishing or spoofed text.
example_prompt: Does this domain/text contain lookalike Unicode characters?
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust check against the Unicode confusables table; no network.
rationale: Security-relevant detection that text-normalize (which only cleans) doesn't surface.

name: unit-price-compare
description: Compare unit prices ($/100g, $/oz, $/unit) across package sizes to find the best deal.
example_prompt: Which is cheaper: 500g for $4.20 or 750g for $6.10?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic + unit normalization; browser-local.
rationale: Unit-price comparison is a practical everyday shopping aid not covered by generic calculators.

name: url-canonicalize
description: Normalize a URL for deduplication: lowercase host, sort/strip query params, resolve dot-segments, drop default ports.
example_prompt: Canonicalize these URLs so I can dedupe them
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM URL parsing/normalization; browser-local.
rationale: URL canonicalization for dedup/SEO is distinct from url-parse's edit-and-rebuild flow.

name: url-diff
description: Fetch two URLs (or two versions of one) and show a readable diff of their text content.
example_prompt: diff the content of these two pages
loader_feasibility: web-fetch loader plus plain Rust diff, client-side.
rationale: Comparing two pages or page versions is a frequent QA and monitoring need.

name: url-status-check
description: Check the HTTP status of a pasted list of URLs and report code, redirects, and timing for each.
example_prompt: Check whether all these links are still alive
loader_feasibility: Fetches each URL via the HTTP host import (as broken-link-check does); in-browser.
rationale: broken-link-check scans one page; bulk-checking an arbitrary URL list is a distinct need.

name: utm-builder
description: Build a campaign tracking URL by adding UTM parameters (source, medium, campaign, term, content).
example_prompt: Add UTM params to my-site.com for a newsletter campaign
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — pure URL string construction, no network needed.
rationale: Marketers build UTM links constantly and the existing url-parse tool only deconstructs them.

name: uuid-inspect
description: Parse a UUID and report its version, variant, and embedded timestamp/node (for v1/v6/v7).
example_prompt: What version is this UUID and when was it made?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM bit parsing; offline.
rationale: uuid-generate only creates them; inspecting an existing one is the inverse dev need.

name: value-counts
description: Count distinct values in a chosen column with counts and percentages.
example_prompt: Show the value counts for the 'country' column in this CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM hash-count; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A pandas value_counts equivalent is a constant first step in data exploration.

name: vat-number-validate
description: Validate an EU VAT number's country format and check digits.
example_prompt: Is VAT number DE123456789 valid?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM per-country checksum rules, offline.
rationale: EU businesses validate VAT IDs often; complements IBAN/card validators.

name: vcard-generate
description: Build a downloadable .vcf vCard contact (name, phone, email, org, address, URL) from supplied fields.
example_prompt: make a vCard for Jane Doe, jane@acme.com, +1 555 0100, Acme Inc
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: text template, no network.
rationale: Directly parallels the backlog's ical-generate and is useful for sharing/printing contacts and QR vCards.

name: vcard-parse
description: Parse a .vcf file into structured contact records (CSV/JSON).
example_prompt: parse this vCard and give me the fields as JSON
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Reading vCards back to data is the inverse of vcard-generate and commonly needed.

name: vector-calc
description: Compute vector operations: dot/cross product, magnitude, angle, normalization, and projection (2D/3D).
example_prompt: what's the cross product of (1,2,3) and (4,5,6)?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Vector math is core to physics/graphics and isn't covered by matrix-calc.

name: venn-diagram
description: Render a 2-3 set Venn diagram with labels and region counts.
example_prompt: Draw a Venn diagram of 120 cat owners, 90 dog owners, 30 both
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM SVG geometry; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Venn diagrams are a frequent explanatory visual not covered by the existing chart set.

name: vesting-calc
description: Generate an equity vesting schedule with cliff and monthly vesting, showing vested shares over time.
example_prompt: vesting schedule for 48,000 options, 4-year vest, 1-year cliff
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM date/share math; local.
rationale: Employees and HR routinely need vesting schedules; no current tool produces them.

name: video-color-lut
description: Apply a 3D color LUT (.cube) to color-grade an entire video.
example_prompt: Apply this cinematic .cube LUT to my video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg lut3d filter; browser-local.
rationale: apply-lut exists only for images; creators want the same cinematic grading on video.

name: video-contact-sheet
description: Generate a thumbnail grid (contact sheet) sampling frames across a video's timeline.
example_prompt: Make a thumbnail grid of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg select+tile filters render a single PNG montage in-browser; chainable into image tools via ref.
rationale: A quick visual overview of a video's contents is handy for previews and reuses the frame-extraction path.

name: video-crossfade
description: Join multiple clips with smooth crossfade/dissolve transitions (and audio crossfade).
example_prompt: Join these three clips with a half-second crossfade between each
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg xfade + acrossfade; browser-local.
rationale: video-concat only hard-cuts; smooth transitions are the most-requested editing upgrade.

name: video-deinterlace
description: Remove interlacing combing artifacts from a video, producing clean progressive frames.
example_prompt: Deinterlace this old camcorder footage
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — yadif/bwdif deinterlace filter runs locally on the decoded stream.
rationale: Old/broadcast footage frequently needs deinterlacing and ffmpeg handles it cleanly.

name: video-denoise
description: Reduce sensor noise/grain in a video while preserving detail.
example_prompt: Clean up the grainy noise in this low-light clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg hqdn3d/nlmeans denoise filters; browser-local.
rationale: Video denoising is distinct from image/audio denoise and a common quality fix for phone footage.

name: video-fade
description: Add fade-in/fade-out (to black) on video and audio at the start and end of a clip.
example_prompt: add a 1-second fade in and fade out to this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (already wired): fade/afade filters, fully in-browser.
rationale: Tiny but constantly wanted polish step, mirroring the backlog's audio-fade.

name: video-fps
description: Change a video's frame rate (e.g. 60→30, or to a fixed fps) with frame drop/duplication.
example_prompt: Convert this 60fps video to 24fps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — fps filter resamples frames locally, no re-shoot needed.
rationale: Frame-rate conversion is a common delivery requirement distinct from speed-change.

name: video-freeze-frame
description: Hold a chosen frame as a still for N seconds within a video (freeze-frame effect).
example_prompt: Freeze the frame at 0:08 for 3 seconds in this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts the frame, builds a still segment, and splices it in.
rationale: A common editing beat for emphasis and reveals not currently offered.

name: video-grid
description: Combine multiple videos into a side-by-side or grid layout playing together.
example_prompt: put these two clips side by side
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg hstack/vstack/xstack.
rationale: Reaction/comparison layouts are common and not covered by sequential concat.

name: video-interpolate
description: Generate smooth slow-motion by interpolating intermediate frames.
example_prompt: make this 30fps clip smooth 120fps slow motion
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime frame-interpolation model (RIFE-class) in-browser.
rationale: AI slow-mo is a sought-after effect distinct from frame-dropping speed changes.

name: video-ken-burns
description: Animate a still image with a smooth pan-and-zoom (Ken Burns) effect into a short video clip.
example_prompt: Make a 5-second slow zoom-in video from this photo
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — zoompan filter generates frames from a single image locally.
rationale: Turning photos into motion is popular for reels/intros and complements the slideshow tool.

name: video-meme-caption
description: Add a top and/or bottom impact-font caption bar to a video clip.
example_prompt: Add the caption 'when the build finally passes' to the top of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg pad + drawtext; browser-local.
rationale: image-meme exists but the video equivalent is just as in-demand for social clips.

name: video-progress-bar
description: Overlay an animated progress/seek bar across the video (social-media style).
example_prompt: Add a progress bar along the bottom of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawbox with time-driven width expression; browser-local.
rationale: Progress-bar overlays are a popular engagement trick for short-form video.

name: video-reverse
description: Play a video (and its audio) backwards.
example_prompt: reverse this clip so it plays backwards
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (already wired): reverse/areverse filters, fully in-browser.
rationale: Popular meme/creative effect with a simple, reliable ffmpeg path.

name: video-split
description: Split a video into fixed-length segments (e.g. every 60s).
example_prompt: split this video into 60-second chunks
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg segment muxer (stream-copy).
rationale: Needed for upload limits and Stories/Shorts; trim only does a single window.

name: video-stabilize
description: Smooth out camera shake in a handheld video using motion-detection stabilization.
example_prompt: stabilize this shaky video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg vidstabdetect+vidstabtransform two-pass; both passes run locally in ffmpeg.
rationale: Stabilization noticeably improves handheld footage and is fully achievable with ffmpeg's vidstab filters.

name: video-strip-metadata
description: Remove embedded metadata (location, device, timestamps) from a video by remuxing it clean.
example_prompt: Strip the GPS and device metadata from this video before I share it
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — stream-copy remux with -map_metadata -1, fast and local.
rationale: Privacy parity with the existing image-strip-metadata tool, which video lacks.

name: video-thumbnail-track
description: Generate a sprite sheet of evenly-spaced thumbnails plus a WebVTT track for scrubbing previews in video players.
example_prompt: make a scrubbing thumbnail sprite and VTT for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg frame sampling plus plain Rust sprite packing, in-browser.
rationale: Web developers need preview thumbnails for custom players and no tool produces the VTT.

name: video-timelapse
description: Turn long footage into a timelapse by dropping frames and speeding it up (drops audio).
example_prompt: Make a 10x timelapse out of this hour-long screen recording
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg select/setpts frame decimation; browser-local.
rationale: Timelapse is a distinct workflow from video-speed (heavy frame drop, no pitch-corrected audio).

name: video-to-webp
description: Convert a video (or trimmed window) into an animated WebP, far smaller than GIF.
example_prompt: Turn this clip into an animated webp
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg encodes animated WebP fully in-browser.
rationale: Modern, smaller alternative to the existing video-to-gif for web use.

name: vin-decode
description: Decode a vehicle VIN into year, country, manufacturer, and check-digit validity.
example_prompt: Decode VIN 1HGCM82633A004352
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM WMI/year tables plus check-digit math, offline.
rationale: VIN decoding is a popular consumer/automotive lookup with no current tool.

name: vlsm-calc
description: Subdivide a network into variable-length subnets sized to required host counts.
example_prompt: VLSM 192.168.1.0/24 into subnets for 50, 20, and 5 hosts
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM allocation algorithm.
